{ For \(a,b\in\mathbb R\), write \(a\wedge b:=\min\{a,b\}\),
\(a\vee b:=\max\{a,b\}\), and \(a^+:=a\vee0\).
For an open set \(U\subset\mathbb R^2\), let \(C^2(U)\) denote the space
of twice continuously differentiable real-valued functions on \(U\).
Its subspace \(C_b^2(U)\) consists of functions that, together with
their first- and second-order partial derivatives, are bounded.
Similarly, \(C_b^\infty(U)\) denotes the space of smooth functions
whose derivatives of every order are bounded.
For vector- or matrix-valued functions, these conventions apply
componentwise.}

label: def:coordinatewise
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:coordinatewise}
	Assume \eqref{eq:boundary-compatible} holds.
	We call \(Z=(Z_t)_{t\ge0}\), with \(Z_t=(X_t,Y_t)\),
	a \emph{coordinatewise process} (CWP)
	if it satisfies the following:
	Before \(\tau_0\wedge\tau_\infty\), it follows
	\eqref{eq:model}. On \(\{\tau_0<\tau_\infty\}\),
	if \(Y\) reaches zero first, then \(Y\) remains zero and
	the surviving coordinate solves
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		X_t={}&X_{\tau_0}
		-\int_{\tau_0}^t b_{10}X_s^{r_{10}}\,\mathrm d s
		+\int_{\tau_0}^t\sqrt{2b_{11}X_s^{r_{11}}}\,\mathrm d B_1(s)\\
		&+\int_{\tau_0}^t\int_0^\infty
		\int_0^{b_{12}X_{s-}^{r_{12}}}
		z\,\widetilde N_1(\,\mathrm d s,\,\mathrm d z,\,\mathrm d u).
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	If \(X\) reaches zero first, then \(X\) remains zero and
	the surviving coordinate solves
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		Y_t={}&Y_{\tau_0}
		-\int_{\tau_0}^t b_{20}Y_s^{r_{20}}\,\mathrm d s
		+\int_{\tau_0}^t\sqrt{2b_{21}Y_s^{r_{21}}}\,\mathrm d B_2(s)\\
		&+\int_{\tau_0}^t\int_0^\infty
		\int_0^{b_{22}Y_{s-}^{r_{22}}}
		z\,\widetilde N_2(\,\mathrm d s,\,\mathrm d z,\,\mathrm d u).
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	If both coordinates are zero, the process remains at the origin.
	On \(\{\tau_\infty\le\tau_0\}\), it is killed at
	\(\tau_\infty\). For a boundary initial state, set
	\(\tau_0=0\) and start the corresponding axis dynamics
	at time zero.

title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:absorbed}
We call \(Z^{\tau_0}=(Z_t^{\tau_0})_{t\ge0}\)
a \emph{source-stopped process} (SSP)
if it satisfies the following: for an initial state in
\(E^\circ\), it follows \eqref{eq:model} up to
\(\tau_0\wedge\tau_\infty\), remains at \(Z_{\tau_0}\)
after \(\tau_0\) on \(\{\tau_0<\tau_\infty\}\), and is
killed at \(\tau_\infty\) on \(\{\tau_\infty\le\tau_0\}\).
For an initial state \((x_0,y_0)\in\partial E\), set
\(\tau_0=0\) and \(Z_t^{\tau_0}=(x_0,y_0)\) for all
\(t\ge0\).
	\(Z_t^{\tau_0}=(x_0,y_0)\) for all \(t\ge0\).

title: Remark
body_md:
Definition \ref{def:absorbed} does not require
	\eqref{eq:boundary-compatible}. When \eqref{eq:boundary-compatible} holds,
	\[
	Z_t^{\tau_0}=Z_{t\wedge\tau_0},
	\qquad t\ge0,
	\]
	where the CWP \(Z\) is the continuation in \Cref{def:coordinatewise},
	with the same killing convention.

Assume that \(\iota_1=\iota_2=0\) and
\Cref{ass:dissipative} holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item A probability \(\pi\) is invariant for the SSP \(Z^{\tau_0}\) if and only if \(\pi(\partial E)=1\).
\item If \eqref{eq:boundary-compatible} holds, then
\(\delta_{(0,0)}\) is the unique invariant probability for
the CWP \(Z\). If, in addition,
\((P_t)_{t\ge0}\) is weak Feller, then for every $(x_0,y_0)\in E$,
\[
 \Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}\Rightarrow\delta_{(0,0)}
 \qquad\text{as }T\to\infty.
\]
\end{enumerate}

\label{thm:competitive-noimm}
Assume that \(\iota_1=\iota_2=0\), \(a_1,a_2<0\), and
\eqref{eq:boundary-compatible} holds.
A probability \(\pi\) is invariant for the SSP \(Z^{\tau_0}\) if and only if \(\pi(\partial E)=1\), and every

concentrated on \(\partial E\).
If, in addition,

 \label{eq:axis-nontrivial}
\end{equation}
then \(\delta_{(0,0)}\) is the unique invariant probability
for the CWP \(Z\). If \((P_t)_{t\ge0}\) is also
weak Feller, then for $(x_0,y_0)\in E$,
\[
 \Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}\Rightarrow\delta_{(0,0)}
 \qquad\text{as }T\to\infty.
\]

body_md:
\label{thm:cooperative-sharp}
Assume \eqref{eq:cooperative-regularity} holds with
\(\iota_1=\iota_2=0\), \(a_1,a_2>0\),
\(\theta_i=\kappa_i=1\), \(r_{i0}>2\), and
\(b_{i1}+b_{i2}>0\), \(i=1,2\).
Suppose that, for some constant \(\beta\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 r_{i1}=2+\beta\quad\text{if }b_{i1}>0,
 \qquad
 r_{i2}=\alpha_i+\beta\quad\text{if }b_{i2}>0,
 \qquad i=1,2.
\]
When \(\beta=1\), define
\[
 \Psi_i(p):=b_{i1}p(p+1)
   +b_{i2}\frac{\Gamma(p+\alpha_i)}
                    {\Gamma(p)\Gamma(\alpha_i)},
 \qquad p>0,\quad i=1,2,
\]
and let \(\widehat q_1,\widehat q_2\in(0,1)\) be the unique solutions of
\begin{eqnarray}\label{q1q2} 
 \Psi_1(\widehat q_1)=a_2(1-\widehat q_1),
 \qquad
 \Psi_2(\widehat q_2)=a_1(1-\widehat q_2).
\end{eqnarray}
For both the CWP \(Z\) and the SSP \(Z^{\tau_0}\),
a nondegenerate invariant probability exists if and only if
\[
 \beta>1
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 \bigl(\beta=1\ \text{and}\ \widehat q_1+\widehat q_2>1\bigr).
\]
Otherwise, the invariant probabilities of the
SSP \(Z^{\tau_0}\) are exactly the probabilities concentrated on
\(\partial E\), whereas \(\delta_{(0,0)}\) is the unique
invariant probability of the CWP \(Z\).

label: eq1005a
title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to consider \(x,y>0\). Let
\[
 u=x^{r_{10}},\quad v=y^{r_{20}},\qquad
 p=\frac{\theta_1}{r_{10}},\quad q=\frac{\kappa_1}{r_{20}},\quad
 r=\frac{\kappa_2}{r_{10}},\quad s=\frac{\theta_2}{r_{20}}.
\]
 By \eqref{eq:weighted-generator-expansion}, 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq1005a}
 \mathcal L V_0(x,y)=\iota_1+c_1\iota_2-b_{10}u-c_1b_{20}v
             +a_1u^pv^q+c_1a_2u^rv^s.
\end{eqnarray}
 If \(a_1,a_2\le0\), every \(c_1>0\) is admissible
and \(C_0=0\). If \(a_1>0>a_2\) and
\eqref{eq:balanced-interactions} holds, the interaction terms
cancel for \(c_1=a_1/(-a_2)\), and again \(C_0=0\).
It remains to consider \(a_1>0\). Suppose first that \(a_2<0\), and set
\[
 \lambda=
 \begin{cases}
 (p/r)\wedge(q/s),&r+s>1,\\
 0,&r+s\le1.
 \end{cases}
\]
By \eqref{eq:mixed-parameter-condition},
\[
 p-\lambda r\ge0,\qquad q-\lambda s\ge0,\qquad
 (p-\lambda r)+(q-\lambda s)+\lambda\le1.
\]
By the above, we have $p -\lambda r < 1$. In fact, 
we have $p -\lambda r \le 1 - \lambda - (q - \lambda s) \le 1 - \lambda < 1$ if $\lambda > 0$; for the case of $\lambda = 0$, since \(q=\kappa_1/r_{20}>0\) by \eqref{eq:imm-regularity}, we have $p \le 1 - q < 1$. By
Young's inequality, one obtains
\begin{eqnarray*} 
 a_1u^pv^q
 \!\!\!&=\!\!\!& a_1u^{p-\lambda r}v^{q-\lambda s}(u^rv^s)^\lambda
\le a_1u^{p-\lambda r}(1+v+u^rv^s)^{q-\lambda s+\lambda}
\cr
 \!\!\!&\le\!\!\!& a_1u^{p-\lambda r}(1+v+u^rv^s)^{1-p+\lambda r} \le  \frac{b_{10}}2u+K(1+v+u^rv^s)
\end{eqnarray*} 
for some \(K>0\). Taking
\(c_1\ge\max\{2K/b_{20},K/|a_2|\}\) in
\eqref{eq:weighted-generator-expansion}, \eqref{eq1005a} yields
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq1005b} 
 \mathcal L V_0(x,y)\le\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+K
 -\frac{b_{10}}2u-\frac{c_1b_{20}}2v.
\end{eqnarray}
When \(a_2=0\), we have
\(p+q\le1\) and \(p<1\) by \eqref{eq:mixed-parameter-condition}. The same argument gives
\(a_1u^pv^q\le(b_{10}/2)u+K(1+v)\), so
\(c_1\ge2K/b_{20}\) yields { the same bound form \eqref{eq1005b}.}
Suppose now that \(a_1,a_2>0\). By
\Cref{ass:cooperative-dissipation}, \(p+q\le1\) and \(r+s\le1\).
For all \(h,k>0\) with \(h+k<1\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq1005c} 
 u^hv^k\le(u+v)^{h+k}\le\varepsilon(u+v)+C_\varepsilon.
\end{eqnarray}
If \(p+q<1\) and \(r+s<1\), take \(c_1=1\).
Applying \eqref{eq1005c} to the last two terms in
\eqref{eq1005a} gives
\[
 \mathcal L V_0(x,y)\le\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0
 -\frac{b_{10}}2u-\frac{c_1b_{20}}2v
\]
for some constant \(C_0\ge0\).
If \(p+q=1>r+s\), by Young's inequality, it gives
	\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq1006a} 
a_1u^pv^q\le(b_{10}/4)u+Kv
\end{eqnarray} 
for some \(K>0\).
Choose \(c_1\ge4K/b_{20}\). Since \(r+s<1\), then by \eqref{eq1005c},
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq1006}
 c_1a_2u^rv^s\le\frac{b_{10}}4u+\frac{c_1b_{20}}4v+C_0
\end{eqnarray}
 for some \(C_0\ge0\).
By \eqref{eq1006a}, \eqref{eq1006} and \eqref{eq1005a}, it proves \eqref{eq:weighted-dissipation}.
The case \(r+s=1>p+q\) follows similarly by using
\(a_2u^rv^s\le Ku+(b_{20}/4)v\) and choosing
\(0<c_1\le b_{10}/(4K)\).
Finally, suppose that \(p+q=r+s=1\), so \(p,q,r,s\in(0,1)\).
Set
\[
 t_0=(a_1/b_{10})^{1/q},\qquad
 c_1=\frac{b_{10}q}{a_2r}t_0^{1-r},\qquad
 F(t)=b_{10}t+c_1b_{20}-a_1t^p-c_1a_2t^r.
\]
Then by \eqref{eq:cooperative-critical} and \eqref{eq:imm-regularity}, it yields $F''(t)>0, F'(t_0)=0$ and $F(t_0)=c_1(b_{20}-a_2t_0^r)>0.$
Hence \(F(t)\ge F(t_0)>0\) for all \(t\ge t_0\). Since
\(F(t)/(1+t)\to b_{10}>0\) as \(t\to\infty\), $c:=\inf_{t\ge0}\frac{F(t)}{1+t}>0.$
By \eqref{eq1005a},
\[
 \mathcal L V_0(x,y)=\iota_1+c_1\iota_2-vF(u/v)
 \le\iota_1+c_1\iota_2-c(u+v).
\]
{ By continuity, the bound holds on \(E\), so
\eqref{eq:weighted-dissipation} follows with \(C_0=0\).}

label: eq:linear-Foster
title: Proof
body_md:
For \(N>0\), set $\tau_N^{V_0}:=\inf\{t\ge0:\ V_0(Z_t)\ge N\}.$
Since \(r_{10},r_{20}>1\), by \eqref{eq:weighted-dissipation}, there exists a constant \(C>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal L V_0+V_0\le C
 \qquad\text{on }E.
 \label{eq:linear-Foster}
\end{equation}
Fix \((x_0,y_0)\in E\). By \eqref{eq:model}, for $0\le t<\tau_\infty,$
\begin{eqnarray}\label{Vito}
 V_0(Z_t)= V_0(x_0,y_0)+\int_0^t\mathcal L V_0(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s+M_t, 
\end{eqnarray}
where \(M=(M_t)_{t\ge0}\) is the local martingale given by
\begin{eqnarray}\label{M} 
 M_t\!\!\!&=\!\!\!& \int_0^t\sqrt{2b_{11}X_s^{r_{11}}}\,\mathrm d B_1(s)
 +c_1\int_0^t\sqrt{2b_{21}Y_s^{r_{21}}}\,\mathrm d B_2(s)  +\int_0^t\int_0^\infty\int_0^{b_{12}X_{s-}^{r_{12}}}
 z\,\widetilde N_1(\,\mathrm d s,\,\mathrm d z,\,\mathrm d u)\cr
 \!\!\!&\!\!\!& +c_1\int_0^t\int_0^\infty\int_0^{b_{22}Y_{s-}^{r_{22}}}
 z\,\widetilde N_2(\,\mathrm d s,\,\mathrm d z,\,\mathrm d u).
\end{eqnarray}
For \(N> V_0(x_0,y_0)\), set $M_t^{(N)}:=\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}}\mathrm e^s\,\mathrm d M_s.$
It is easy to see that \(\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}M_t^{(N)}=0\).
By integration by parts, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
 \mathrm e^{t\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}}V_0(Z_{t\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}})
 = V_0({x_0,y_0})+\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}}\mathrm e^s
 \bigl(V_0+\mathcal L  V_0\bigr)(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s +M_t^{(N)}.
\end{eqnarray*} 
Using \eqref{eq:linear-Foster} and taking expectations, we obtain
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_{{x_0,y_0}}\left[
 \mathrm e^{t\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}}V_0(Z_{t\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}})
 \right]
 \le V_0({x_0,y_0})+C(\mathrm e^t-1).
 \label{eq:exp-V-stopped}
\end{equation}
On \(\{\tau_N^{V_0}\le t\}\), we have $V_0(Z_{t\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}})\ge N.$
It follows that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{{x_0,y_0}}(\tau_N^{V_0}\le t)
 \le\frac{V_0({x_0,y_0})+C(\mathrm e^t-1)}{N}.
 \label{eq:nonexplosion-prob}
\end{equation}
Since
\begin{eqnarray}\label{star} 
 1+(1\wedge c_1)(x\vee y)
 \le V_0(x,y)
 \le 1+(1+c_1)(x\vee y),
\end{eqnarray}
we have \(\tau_N^{V_0}\uparrow\tau_\infty\).
Letting \(N\to\infty\) in \eqref{eq:nonexplosion-prob}
gives \(\mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(\tau_\infty\le t)=0\) for every
\(t>0\). Thus the solution to \eqref{eq:model} is nonexplosive.
By \eqref{star}, we obtain $
 \{\tau_R^+\le t\}
 \subset\{\tau_{1+(1\wedge c_1)R}^{V_0}\le t\}.$
By \eqref{eq:nonexplosion-prob}, for every compact \(K\subset E\)
and all sufficiently large \(R\), we have
\[
 \sup_{(x_0,y_0)\in K}\mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(\tau_R^+\le t)
 \le
 \frac{\sup_{(x_0,y_0)\in K}V_0(x_0,y_0)
 +C(\mathrm e^t-1)}{1+(1\wedge c_1)R}
 \rightarrow0\qquad\text{as }R\to\infty.
\]
Letting \(N\to\infty\) in \eqref{eq:exp-V-stopped}, using Fatou's
lemma, and dividing by \({\mathrm e^t}\), it yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{{x_0,y_0}}V_0(Z_t)
 \le\mathrm e^{-t}V_0({x_0,y_0})
 +C(1-\mathrm e^{-t}),
 \qquad t\ge0.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:V-first-moment}.
Finally, by stopping \eqref{Vito} at \(T\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}\)
and taking expectations, we have
\begin{align*}
 &\mathbb E_{{x_0,y_0}}V_0(Z_{T\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}})
 +\mathbb E_{{x_0,y_0}}\int_0^{T\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}}
 \bigl(\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0-\mathcal L V_0(Z_s)\bigr)\,\mathrm d s\\
 &\hspace{25mm}=V_0({x_0,y_0})+
 \left(\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0\right)
 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}(T\wedge\tau_N^{V_0}).
\end{align*}
By \eqref{eq:weighted-dissipation},
\(\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0-\mathcal L V_0\ge0\).
Letting \(N\to\infty\) and applying Fatou's lemma, we obtain
\eqref{eq:imm-occupation-bound}.
The result follows.

body_md:
\label{lem:common-stationary-moments}
	Assume that \eqref{eq:imm-regularity} and
	\Cref{ass:weighted-dissipation} hold.
	Let \(c_1,c>0\) and \(C_0\ge0\)
	satisfy \eqref{eq:weighted-dissipation}.
	If \(\pi\) is an invariant probability for the
	nonnegative solution $Z$ of \eqref{eq:model}, then
	\[
	\left\{
	\begin{aligned}
		&\int_E\bigl(\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0-\mathcal L V_0(x, y)\bigr)\pi(\,\mathrm d x, \,\mathrm d y)
		\le \iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0,\\
		&\int_E W_0(x,y) \pi(\,\mathrm d x, \,\mathrm d y)
		\le \frac{\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0}{c}<\infty.
	\end{aligned}
	\right.
	\]

label: eq:stationary-truncated-drift-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
To avoid assuming any moment
	condition on \(\pi\), we first use the bounded functions
	\[
	f_n(x,y):=n\bigl(1-e^{- V_0(x,y)/n}\bigr),
	\qquad n\ge1.
	\]
The function \(v\mapsto n(1-e^{-v/n})\) is concave.
By \eqref{eq:generator}, it is easy to check that
	\[
	\mathcal L f_n(x, y)\le e^{-V_0(x, y)/n}\mathcal L V_0(x, y).
	\]
For each fixed \(n\), both \(\mathcal L f_n\) and
\(e^{- V_0/n}\mathcal L V_0\) are bounded on \(E\).
	By \Cref{lem:imm-lyapunov}, the solution $Z$ is nonexplosive.
	Since \(f_n\) and \(\mathcal L f_n\) are bounded, localized
	It\^o's formula and bounded convergence yield, for \(t>0\),
	\[
	\mathbb E_\pi f_n(Z_t)-\mathbb E_\pi f_n(Z_0)
	=\int_0^t\mathbb E_\pi\mathcal L f_n(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s.
	\]
Hence, by stationarity, we obtain
	\[
	0=\int_E\mathcal L f_n\,\,\mathrm d\pi
	\le\int_E e^{-V_0/n} \mathcal L V_0(x, y) \,\,\mathrm d\pi.
	\]
Since \(0<e^{- V_0/n}\le1\), it follows that
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:stationary-truncated-drift-bound}
\!\!\!&\!\!\!& \int_E  {e^{-V_0(x,y)/n}}
 \bigl(\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0- {\mathcal L V_0(x,y)}\bigr)\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)\cr
 \!\!\!&\!\!\!&\qquad\le(\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0)
 \int_E e^{- V_0(x,y)/n}\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)
 \le\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0.
\end{eqnarray}
	By \eqref{eq:weighted-dissipation}, we have 
	\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq2} 
	\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0-\mathcal L  V_0(x, y)
	\ge c W_0(x,y) \ge0.
	\end{eqnarray}
 Letting \(n\to\infty\) in \eqref{eq:stationary-truncated-drift-bound}
and applying Fatou's lemma, we obtain
	\begin{equation}
	\int_E
	\bigl(\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0-\mathcal L V_0(x, y)\bigr)\pi(\,\mathrm d x, \,\mathrm d y)
	\le \iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0.
	\label{eq:stationary-integrated-drift-bound}
\end{equation}
	Combining \eqref{eq2} and \eqref{eq:stationary-integrated-drift-bound}, we obtain
	\[
	\int_E W_0(x,y) \pi(\,\mathrm d x, \,\mathrm d y)
	\le\frac{\iota_1+c_1\iota_2+C_0}{c}<\infty.
	\]
	The result follows.

label: lem:time-average-limits
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:time-average-limits}
Let \(D=E\) or \(E^\circ\), and let \((Q_t)_{t\ge0}\)
be the transition semigroup of a conservative weak Feller
Markov process with c\`adl\`ag paths in \(D\).
For \(z\in D\), define
\[
\nu_T^z:=\frac1T\int_0^T Q_s(z,\cdot)\,\mathrm d s.
\]
Then every weak subsequential limit of \(\nu_T^z\) as
\(T\to\infty\) is invariant for \((Q_t)_{t\ge0}\).
If \(\{\nu_T^z:T\ge1\}\) is tight on \(D\), an invariant
probability exists. If, in addition, the invariant probability
is unique, say \(\pi\), then
\(\nu_T^z\Rightarrow\pi\) as \(T\to\infty\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use the Krylov--Bogoliubov argument; see
\cite[Theorem~3.1.1, p.~21]{DaPratoZabczyk1996}.
For \(t\ge0\) and \(f\in C_b(D)\), the semigroup property gives
\begin{eqnarray*}
 \left|\int_D Q_tf\,\,\mathrm d\nu_T^z-\int_D f\,\,\mathrm d\nu_T^z\right|
 =\frac1T\left|
 \int_T^{T+t}Q_sf(z)\,\mathrm d s-\int_0^tQ_sf(z)\,\mathrm d s
 \right| \le\frac{2t\|f\|_\infty}{T}.
 \end{eqnarray*}
If \(\nu_{T_k}^z\Rightarrow\pi\) for some \(T_k\to\infty\),
the weak Feller property allows passage to the limit,
yielding
\[
 \int_D Q_tf\,\,\mathrm d\pi=\int_D f\,\,\mathrm d\pi.
\]
Thus \(\pi\) is invariant. Tightness and Prokhorov's theorem
give such a subsequential limit. If the invariant probability
is unique, every weak subsequential limit equals \(\pi\). Then by tightness, we have  \(\nu_T^z\Rightarrow\pi\). The result follows.

label: eq:strict-positive-generator
title: Proof
body_md:
Observe that
\[
 f_x'(x,y)=f_{xx}''(x,y)=0,\qquad
 f_y'(x,y)=-\mathrm e^{-y},\qquad
 f_{yy}''(x,y)=\mathrm e^{-y},
\]
and
\(f(x,y+z)-f(x,y)-zf_y'(x,y)
=\mathrm e^{-y}(\mathrm e^{-z}-1+z)\).
Since
\[
 {\int_0^\infty(\mathrm e^{-z}-1+z)\,\mu_2(\,\mathrm d z)
 =\frac1{\Gamma(\alpha_2)}},
\]
then it follows from \eqref{eq:generator} that, for \((x,y)\in E^\circ\),
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal L f(x,y)
  =\mathrm e^{-y}\left[
 -a_2y^{\theta_2}x^{\kappa_2}
 +b_{20}y^{r_{20}}+b_{21}y^{r_{21}}
 +\frac{b_{22}}{\Gamma(\alpha_2)}y^{r_{22}}\right] \ge -a_2\mathrm e^{-y}y^{\theta_2}x^{\kappa_2}>0.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:strict-positive-generator}
\end{equation}
We first consider the SSP $Z^{\tau_0}$ started from
\((x_0,y_0)\in E^\circ\).
For every sufficiently large integer \(k\),
\eqref{eq:localized-dynkin-martingale} and \(\mathcal L f\ge0\) imply that $(f(Z_{t\wedge\tau_{1/k}^-\wedge\tau_k^+}))_{t\ge0}$
is a bounded submartingale.
By conservativeness and \Cref{def:absorbed}, for every fixed \(t\ge0\),
\[
 \lim_{k\to\infty}
 f(Z_{t\wedge\tau_{1/k}^-\wedge\tau_k^+})
 =f(Z_t^{\tau_0})
 \qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Since \(0<f\le1\), by dominated convergence in the conditional submartingale inequality, one sees that 
\((f(Z_t^{\tau_0}))_{t\ge0}\) is a bounded submartingale.
For the CWP, \eqref{eq:boundary-compatible}
ensures that all coefficients attached to an extinct
coordinate vanish at zero, so that keeping this coordinate
at zero is consistent with \eqref{eq:model}.
The preceding argument applies up to \(\tau_0\).
On the \(x\)-axis, \(f\equiv1\), while on the open
\(y\)-axis, since \(\kappa_2>0\),
\begin{equation}
\mathcal L f(0,y)=e^{-y}\left[
b_{20}y^{r_{20}}+b_{21}y^{r_{21}}
+\frac{b_{22}}{\Gamma(\alpha_2)}y^{r_{22}}
\right]\ge0.
\label{eq:axis-laplace-generator}
\end{equation}
Localization along the axes and the strong Markov property
from \Cref{prop:axis-realization} therefore show that
\((f(Z_t))_{t\ge0}\) is a bounded
submartingale.
Thus, under either convention,
\begin{equation}
 Q_tf(x_0,y_0)\ge f(x_0,y_0),
 \qquad (x_0,y_0)\in E,\quad t\ge0.
 \label{eq:laplace-subinvariant}
\end{equation}
Fix \((x_0,y_0)\in E^\circ\), \(t>0\),
\(0<\varepsilon<x_0\wedge y_0\), and \(N>x_0\vee y_0\).
{Right continuity gives}
\(\mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(\tau_\varepsilon^-\wedge\tau_N^+>0)=1\).
Moreover, by \eqref{eq:strict-positive-generator}, we have $c_0:=\min_{(x,y)\in[\varepsilon,N]^2}\mathcal L f(x,y)>0.$
It follows from \eqref{eq:localized-dynkin-martingale} that
\begin{eqnarray*}
 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}f(Z_{t\wedge\tau_\varepsilon^-\wedge\tau_N^+})
 -f(x_0,y_0) \!\!\!&=\!\!\!& \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_\varepsilon^-\wedge\tau_N^+}
               \mathcal L f(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s\cr
 \!\!\!&\ge\!\!\!& c_0\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}
        (t\wedge\tau_\varepsilon^-\wedge\tau_N^+)>0.
\end{eqnarray*} 
By optional sampling for the bounded submartingale, one sees that
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq0911} 
 Q_tf(x_0,y_0)
 \ge\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}f(Z_{t\wedge\tau_\varepsilon^-\wedge\tau_N^+})
 >f(x_0,y_0).
\end{eqnarray}
{By \eqref{eq:laplace-subinvariant} and \eqref{eq0911},
\(Q_tf-f\) is nonnegative on \(E\) and strictly positive on
\(E^\circ\) for every \(t>0\).}  If \(\pi\) is invariant, then $\int_E(Q_tf-f)\,\mathrm d\pi=0,$
which forces \(\pi(E^\circ)=0\). The result follows.

label: prop:noimm-classification
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:noimm-classification}
{Assume that \(\iota_1=\iota_2=0\) and {\(a_2<0\)}.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If the SSP $Z^{\tau_0}$ is conservative, then a
probability \(\pi\) is invariant for \((P_t^{\tau_0})\) if and only if
\(\pi(\partial E)=1\).
\item Assume \eqref{eq:boundary-compatible} and that the
CWP $Z$ is conservative.
{Then every invariant probability \(\pi\) for
\((P_t)\) satisfies \(\pi(\partial E)=1\).}  If, in addition,
\eqref{eq:axis-nontrivial} holds,
then \(\delta_{(0,0)}\) is its unique invariant probability.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\noindent\textup{(i)}
By \Cref{def:absorbed}, we have $P_t^{\tau_0}((x_0,y_0),\cdot)=\delta_{(x_0,y_0)}$ for
every $(x_0,y_0)\in\partial E$ and $t\ge0.$
If \(\pi(\partial E)=1\), then, for every \(h\in B_b(E)\),
\[
 \int_E P_t^{\tau_0}h\,\mathrm d\pi
 =\int_{\partial E}h(u,v)\pi(\,\mathrm d u,\,\mathrm d v)
 =\int_Eh\,\mathrm d\pi.
\]
Thus \(\pi\) is invariant.  Conversely,
\Cref{lem:interior-exclusion} shows that every invariant probability
\(\pi\) satisfies \(\pi(\partial E)=1\).


\textup{(ii)}
Let \(\pi\) be invariant for \((P_t)_{t\ge0}\).
By \Cref{lem:interior-exclusion}, we have \(\pi(\partial E)=1\). Assume now that \eqref{eq:axis-nontrivial} holds,
and let \(f\) be as in \Cref{lem:interior-exclusion}.
By \eqref{eq:laplace-subinvariant}, \(P_tf\ge f\) on \(E\).
By \eqref{eq:axis-laplace-generator} and \eqref{eq:axis-nontrivial}, we have \(\mathcal L f(0,y)>0\) for every \(y>0\).
Similar to the argument in \eqref{eq0911}, we obtain
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq0911a}
 P_tf(x_0,y_0)>f(x_0,y_0)\quad\text{if }y_0>0,\qquad
 P_tf(x_0,0)=f(x_0,0)=1,
 \qquad t>0.
\end{eqnarray}
{By invariance of \(\pi\),}
\(\int_E(P_tf-f)\,\mathrm d\pi=0\). By \eqref{eq0911a}, we have 
\(\pi([0,\infty)\times\{0\})=1\).
Set \(g(x,y):=\mathrm e^{-x}\). Similar to \eqref{eq0911a},
\[
 P_tg(x_0,0)>g(x_0,0)\quad\text{if }x_0>0,\qquad
 P_tg(0,0)=g(0,0)=1,\qquad t>0.
\]
Since \(\pi([0,\infty)\times\{0\})=1\), it yields
\[
 0=\int_{(0,\infty)\times\{0\}}
       \bigl(P_tg(u,0)-g(u,0)\bigr)\pi(\,\mathrm d u,\,\mathrm d v).
\]
Thus \(\pi((0,\infty)\times\{0\})=0\) and
\(\pi=\delta_{(0,0)}\). Hence \(\delta_{(0,0)}\) is invariant.

label: eq:cw-preboundary-Foster
title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{lem:predator-source-occupation}, the model
\eqref{eq:model} is source-conservative. By
\Cref{prop:axis-realization}, $\mathbb{P}_{x_0, y_0}(\tau_\infty = \infty) = 1$ for every $(x_0, y_0) \in E$. Then the
CWP $Z$ is conservative. For \((x_0,y_0)\in E^\circ\), apply
\eqref{eq:localized-dynkin-inequality} to \(H\), use
\eqref{eq:Foster-H}, and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) and
\(N\to\infty\). By Fatou's lemma and monotone convergence, we have
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:cw-preboundary-Foster}
		\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}H(Z_{t\wedge\tau_0})
		+c\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_0}
		W(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s \le H(x_0,y_0)+C\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}(t\wedge\tau_0).
	\end{eqnarray}
In particular,
\begin{eqnarray*} 
\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\!\left[
H(Z_{t\wedge\tau_0})
\1_{\{\tau_0\le t\}}\right]\le H(x_0,y_0)+Ct.
\end{eqnarray*}
By \eqref{eq:generator} and
\cite[Lemma~A.3]{JiXiongXuYang2026}, for \(x>0\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal L H(x,0)
 = -b_{10}x^{q_1+r_{10}-1}
 +(q_1-1)b_{11}x^{q_1+r_{11}-2}+\frac{(q_1-1)\Gamma(\alpha_1-q_1)}
 {\Gamma(\alpha_1)\Gamma(2-q_1)}
 b_{12}x^{q_1+r_{12}-\alpha_1}.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:predator-axis-generator}
\end{equation}
If \(q_1\le1\), the last two terms on the right-hand side of
\eqref{eq:predator-axis-generator} are nonpositive.
If \(q_1>1\), by \Cref{ass:dissipative} and
\eqref{eq:dissipative-dominance}, we have $
0\le q_1+r_{11}-2<q_1+r_{10}-1$ if $b_{11}>0,$
and $0\le q_1+r_{12}-\alpha_1<q_1+r_{10}-1$ if
$b_{12}>0.$
Since \(b_{10}>0\), there exist constants  {\(C_1\ge0\) and \(c_1>0\)}
such that
\begin{eqnarray*} 
 {\mathcal L H(x,0)\le C_1-c_1x^{q_1+r_{10}-1}=C_1-c_1W(x,0),\qquad x>0.}
\end{eqnarray*}
Similarly, there exist constants \(C_2\ge0\) and \(c_2>0\) such that
\begin{eqnarray*} 
 {\mathcal L H(0,y)\le C_2-c_2y^{q_2+r_{20}-1}=C_2-c_2W(0,y),\qquad y>0.}
\end{eqnarray*}
Enlarge \(C\) to \(\max\{C,C_1,C_2\}\) and decrease \(c\) to
\(\min\{c,c_1,c_2\}\).
For an initial state on either open axis, apply It\^o's formula
after stopping the surviving coordinate on \([1/k,k]\), and let
\(k\to\infty\). Fatou's lemma and monotone convergence give
\eqref{eq:cw-global-Foster} for boundary initial states.
At \((0,0)\), the estimate is immediate because the process is constant.
 

On \(\{\tau_0\le t\}\), the process reaches the boundary
at time \(\tau_0\). Applying the strong Markov property
at \(\tau_0\) and the boundary estimate over the remaining
time \(t-\tau_0\), we obtain
\[
	 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\left[
	\1_{\{\tau_0\le t\}}
	\left\{H(Z_t)
	+c\int_{t\wedge\tau_0}^t
	W(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s\right\}\right] 
	 \le
	\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\left[
	\1_{\{\tau_0\le t\}}
	H(Z_{t\wedge\tau_0})
	\right]
	+C\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}(t-\tau_0)^+.
\]
On \(\{\tau_0>t\}\), we have \(t\wedge\tau_0=t\), so
the occupation integral above vanishes and $
H(Z_t)
=H(Z_{t\wedge\tau_0}).$
Adding the contribution from \(\{\tau_0>t\}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
	 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}H(Z_t)
	+c\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_{t\wedge\tau_0}^t
	W(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s \le
	\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}H(Z_{t\wedge\tau_0})
	+C\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}(t-\tau_0)^+.
\end{aligned}
\]
Adding the occupation integral up to \(t\wedge\tau_0\)
and using \eqref{eq:cw-preboundary-Foster}, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
	&\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}H(Z_t)
	+c\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_0^t
	W(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s\\
	&\qquad\le H(x_0,y_0)
	+C\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\bigl[(t\wedge\tau_0)+(t-\tau_0)^+\bigr]
	=H(x_0,y_0)+Ct.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:cw-global-Foster}, which also gives, for \(T\ge1\),
\[
 \int_E W(u,v)\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}(\,\mathrm d u,\,\mathrm d v)
 \le\frac{H(x_0,y_0)}{cT}+\frac Cc.
\]
Since \(\{(x,y)\in E:W(x,y)\le R\}\) is compact
for every \(R>0\), the preceding bound and Markov's
inequality imply tightness.

label: lem:abs-tightness
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:abs-tightness}
Suppose that \Cref{ass:dissipative} holds.
Then, for every \((x_0,y_0)\in E\), the family
\(\{\Pi_T^{\tau_0,(x_0,y_0)}:T\ge1\}\) is tight.
If \((P_t^{\tau_0})_{t\ge0}\) is weak Feller, every weak limit
as \(T\to\infty\) is invariant and concentrated on \(\partial E\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
{ For \((x_0,y_0)\in\partial E\), the SSP satisfies
	\(Z_t^{\tau_0}=(x_0,y_0)\) for all \(t\ge0\), so $
	\Pi_T^{\tau_0,(x_0,y_0)}=\delta_{(x_0,y_0)}$ for $T>0.$ The conclusion is therefore immediate on \(\partial E\).
	It suffices to consider \((x_0,y_0)\in E^\circ\).}
For \(R>0\), let
\(K_R:=\{(u,v)\in E:W(u,v)\le R\}\), which is compact.
Define
\[
 Z_\partial:=
 \begin{cases}
 Z_{\tau_0},&\tau_0<\tau_\infty,\\
 (0,0),&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then \(Z_\partial\) is an \(E\)-valued random variable, so its law is tight.
Given \(\varepsilon>0\), choose a compact \(K_\partial\subset E\)
such that
\(\mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(Z_\partial\notin K_\partial)
<\varepsilon/2\).
Choose \(R>0\) such that
\((C+H(x_0,y_0))/(cR)<\varepsilon/2\), where \(C,c\) are the
constants in \eqref{eq:source-occupation}.
Observe that, almost surely,
\begin{eqnarray*} 
 \1_{\{Z_s^{\tau_0}\notin K_\partial\cup K_R\}}\le
 \1_{\{s<\tau_0\}}\1_{\{W(Z_s^{\tau_0})>R\}}
 +\1_{\{s\ge\tau_0\}}
  \1_{\{Z_\partial\notin K_\partial\}}.
 \end{eqnarray*} 
Observe that, for \(T\ge1\), \eqref{eq:source-occupation} now gives
\begin{align*}
 \Pi_T^{\tau_0,(x_0,y_0)}((K_\partial\cup K_R)^c)
 &\le\frac1T\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_0^{T\wedge\tau_0}
       \1_{\{W(Z_s)>R\}}\,\mathrm d s
   +\mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(Z_\partial\notin K_\partial)\\
 &\le\frac1{TR}\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_0^{T\wedge\tau_0}
       W(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\\
 &\le\frac{C+H(x_0,y_0)}{cR}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}
 <\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
Thus \(\{\Pi_T^{\tau_0,(x_0,y_0)}:T\ge1\}\) is tight.
Under the weak Feller assumption,
\Cref{lem:time-average-limits} shows that every weak limit
is invariant; it is concentrated on \(\partial E\) by
\Cref{prop:noimm-classification}. The result follows.

label: eq3
title: Proof
body_md:
Take \(c_1=1\) in $S$, which is given by \eqref{SVW}. By \eqref{eq:generator}, we have
	\[
	\mathcal L S(x,y)=a_1x^{\theta_1}y^{\kappa_1}
	+a_2y^{\theta_2}x^{\kappa_2}
	-b_{10}x^{r_{10}}-b_{20}y^{r_{20}}\le0.
	\]
For \((x_0,y_0)\in E^\circ\), by \eqref{eq:localized-dynkin-inequality} and
Fatou's lemma, one sees that
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq3} 
 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}S(Z_{t\wedge\tau_N^+\wedge\tau_0})\le x_0+y_0.
\end{eqnarray}
On \(\{\tau_N^+\le t\wedge\tau_0\}\), \(S(Z_{t\wedge\tau_N^+\wedge\tau_0})\ge N\). Hence
	\[
	\mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(\tau_N^+\le t\wedge\tau_0)
	\le\frac{x_0+y_0}{N},
	\qquad t\ge0,\quad N>x_0\vee y_0.
	\]
	Letting \(N\to\infty\) excludes explosion before or at
	\(\tau_0\). Thus both realizations are conservative by
	Definition~\ref{def:absorbed} and
	Proposition~\ref{prop:axis-realization}.
	By \eqref{eq3} and Fatou's lemma, for every \((x_0,y_0)\in E\), one sees that
	$\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\bigl[X_{t\wedge\tau_0}+Y_{t\wedge\tau_0}\bigr]
		\le x_0+y_0$ and $\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\bigl[X_t+Y_t\bigr]
		\le x_0+y_0$ for $t \ge 0.$
	Consequently, both families of time-averaged transition
	probabilities are tight by Markov's inequality.
	The classification of invariant probabilities follows
	from \Cref{prop:noimm-classification}.
	Under \eqref{eq:axis-nontrivial}, the CWP $Z$ has the unique invariant probability
	\(\delta_{(0,0)}\).
	If its semigroup \((P_t)_{t\ge0}\) is also weak Feller, by
	\Cref{lem:time-average-limits}, $
	\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}\Rightarrow\delta_{(0,0)}$ as $T\to\infty$ for any $(x_0,y_0)\in E.$
	The proof ends here.

For \(i=1,2\), \(u>0\), and \(q<1\),
\[
 \int_0^\infty\bigl[(u+z)^q-u^q-qu^{q-1}z\bigr]\mu_i(\,\mathrm d z)

        {\Gamma(\alpha_i)\Gamma(2-q)}\,u^{q-\alpha_i}.

 \int_0^\infty\bigl[(u+z)^{-p}-u^{-p}+pu^{-p-1}z\bigr]

 =\frac{\Gamma(p+\alpha_i)}{\Gamma(p)\Gamma(\alpha_i)}
       u^{-p-\alpha_i}.
\]

{Assume \eqref{eq:cooperative-regularity},
\(r_{10},r_{20}>1\), and \(\iota_1=\iota_2=0\).} Suppose that
\[
 V(x,y)=S(x,y)+G(x,y),

where \(G\in C^2(E^\circ)\) is nonnegative and nonincreasing
in each variable and $S$ is given by \eqref{SVW}. Let \(W:E^\circ\to[0,\infty)\) be continuous.

\[
 \{(x,y)\in E^\circ:V(x,y)\le M\},\qquad
 \{(x,y)\in E^\circ:W(x,y)\le M\}
\]
are compact subsets of \(E^\circ\), and that
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal L V\le C-cW\qquad\text{on }E^\circ
 \label{eq:interior-lyapunov-drift}
\end{equation}
holds for some \(C,c>0\). Then the CWP \(Z\) solving \eqref{eq:model}
with initial state \((x_0,y_0)\in E^\circ\) is global and remains in
\(E^\circ\) almost surely.
Its restricted semigroup is weak Feller, its time-averaged
transition laws are tight on \(E^\circ\), and every subsequential
limit is an invariant probability \(\pi\) satisfying
{\(\pi(E^\circ)=1\) and}
\(\int_{E^\circ}W\,\mathrm d\pi\le C/c\).

label: eq:interior-exit-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \((x_0,y_0)\in E^\circ\), and, for all sufficiently large
\(n\), set
\[
 \tau_n=\inf\{t\ge0:Z_t\notin(n^{-1},n)^2\},
 \qquad
 v_n=\inf_{(x,y)\in E^\circ\setminus(n^{-1},n)^2}V(x,y).
\]
For every \(M>0\), compactness places \(\{V\le M\}\) inside
\((n^{-1},n)^2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\); hence
\(v_n\ge M\) eventually and \(v_n\to\infty\) as $n \rightarrow \infty$.
Before \(\tau_n\), the Brownian and small-jump integrands have
bounded quadratic norms. For a positive jump of size \(z\)
in coordinate \(i\), nonnegativity and monotonicity of \(G\)
give
\[
 |V(x+z,y)-V(x,y)|\le z+G(x,y),\qquad
 |V(x,y+z)-V(x,y)|\le c_1z+G(x,y).
\]
Thus the large-jump increments and their compensators are
integrable before \(\tau_n\), since \(G\) and the jump rates
are bounded on \([n^{-1},n]^2\) and
\(\int_1^\infty z\,\mu_i(\,\mathrm d z)<\infty\).
By \eqref{eq:interior-lyapunov-drift} and
\eqref{eq:localized-dynkin-inequality}, we obtain
\[
 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}V(Z_{t\wedge\tau_n})
 +c\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_n}W(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s
 \le V(x_0,y_0)+Ct.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(\tau_n\le t)
 \le\frac{V(x_0,y_0)+Ct}{v_n}\rightarrow0
\label{eq:interior-exit-bound}
\end{equation}
as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Thus the CWP \(Z\) is global and remains in
	\(E^\circ\) almost surely, proving the first assertion. Hence by $\tau_n \uparrow \infty$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ and Fatou's lemma, it follows that
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}V(Z_t)
 +c\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_0^tW(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s
 \le V(x_0,y_0)+Ct.
\end{equation*}
In particular, the time-averaged law
\(\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \int_{E^\circ}W(x, y)\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}(\,\mathrm d x, \,\mathrm d y)
 \le\frac{V(x_0,y_0)}{cT}+\frac Cc.
\label{eq:interior-time-average-bound}
\end{equation}
The compact sublevel sets of \(W\) give tightness
of \(\{\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}:T\ge1\}\) on \(E^\circ\).
To prove the weak Feller property, let \(z_k\to z\) in
\(E^\circ\) and couple the CWP \(Z^{(k)}\) and the CWP \(Z\) with the same driving noises. Stop both when
either leaves \((n^{-1},n)^2\), at a time denoted by
\(\sigma_n^{(k)}\). The argument yielding
\eqref{eq:stopped-L1-continuity}, with additional stopping
when either solution reaches the lower boundary of
\((n^{-1},n)^2\), gives
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq4} 
 \mathbb E\bigl|Z^{(k)}_{t\wedge\sigma_n^{(k)}}
          -Z_{t\wedge\sigma_n^{(k)}}\bigr|_1
 \le e^{C_nt}|z_k-z|_1,
\end{eqnarray}
where \(|(x,y)|_1:=|x|+|y|\).
For \(K=\{z,z_k:k\ge1\}\), \eqref{eq:interior-exit-bound} gives
\[
 \mathbb P(\sigma_n^{(k)}\le t)
 \le \frac{2\bigl(\sup_{w\in K}V(w)+Ct\bigr)}{v_n}.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq4} and
uniform continuity of $f$ on \([n^{-1},n]^2\), it implies
\(P_tf(z_k)\to P_tf(z)\) for \(f\in C_b(E^\circ)\),
first letting \(k\to\infty\) and then \(n\to\infty\).
Applying \Cref{lem:time-average-limits} with
\(D=E^\circ\) shows that every weak limit is invariant for
the common interior process, and hence for both boundary realizations.
As a probability on \(E^\circ\), its extension to \(E\)
satisfies \(\pi(E^\circ)=1\).
Taking \(T=T_k\to\infty\) along the convergent subsequence
in \eqref{eq:interior-time-average-bound} gives
\[
 \int_{E^\circ}W\,\,\mathrm d\pi
 \le\liminf_{k\to\infty}
 \int_{E^\circ}W\,\,\mathrm d\Pi_{T_k}^{(x_0,y_0)}
 \le C/c.
\]
The result follows.

label: eq:critical-extinction-integral
title: Proof
body_md:
The assumptions imply \(r_{10},r_{20}>1\), and hence
	\eqref{eq:imm-regularity} and
	\Cref{ass:weighted-dissipation}\textup{(iii)} hold.
	By \Cref{lem:imm-lyapunov}, the CWP \(Z\) is conservative. By \Cref{lem:parameter-drift}, choose \(c_1,c>0\)
so that \eqref{eq:weighted-dissipation} holds with \(C_0=0\).
Fix \((x_0,y_0)\in E\), and set
\(S_t:=S(Z_t)\), with \(S\) defined in \eqref{SVW}.
Since \(S=V_0-1\), \eqref{Vito} yields
\[
 S_t=S(x_0,y_0)+\int_0^t\mathcal L S(Z_s)\,\,\mathrm d s+M_t \quad \text{and} 
 \quad \mathcal L S\le-cW_0\le0.
\]
Thus \((S_t)_{t\ge0}\) is a nonnegative supermartingale. As in the proof of \Cref{lem:imm-lyapunov},
stopping at \(\tau_N^+\) and letting \(N\to\infty\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}S_t
 +c\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_0^t
   W_0(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s
 \le S(x_0,y_0).
\]
Consequently, $ S_t\rightarrow S_\infty<\infty$ almost surely, and 
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}\int_0^\infty
   W_0(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s
 \le\frac{S(x_0,y_0)}{c}.
\label{eq:critical-extinction-integral}
\end{equation}
For every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \inf_{\substack{(x,y)\in E\\ S(x,y)\ge\varepsilon}}
       W_0(x,y)>0.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:critical-extinction-integral},
this implies \(S_\infty=0\) almost surely and yields a sequence
\(t_n\uparrow\infty\) such that $\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}
 W_0(Z_{t_n})
 \rightarrow0.$
By H\"older's inequality, 
\[
 \mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}S_{t_n}
 \le\bigl(\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}(X_{t_n})^{r_{10}}\bigr)^{1/r_{10}}
   +c_1\bigl(\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}(Y_{t_n})^{r_{20}}\bigr)^{1/r_{20}}
 \rightarrow0
\]
as $n \rightarrow \infty$.
Since \(t\mapsto\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}S_t\) is nonincreasing,
\(\mathbb E_{x_0,y_0}S_t\to0\) as \(t\to\infty\). Together with \(S_t\to0\) almost
surely and \(x+y\le\max\{1,c_1^{-1}\}S(x,y)\), we obtain that $
 Z_t\rightarrow(0,0)$ almost surely and in $L^1$ as $t \rightarrow \infty$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:cooperative-regularity} and
	\eqref{eq:cooperative-powers}, we have \(r_{i0}>1\)
	for \(i=1,2\). Hence \eqref{eq:imm-regularity} and
	\Cref{ass:weighted-dissipation}\textup{(iii)} hold.
	By \Cref{lem:imm-lyapunov}, the CWP \(Z\) is conservative. The SSP \(Z^{\tau_0}\)
is then conservative as well.
By \Cref{def:coordinatewise,def:absorbed}, \(\partial E\) is invariant
for both processes. We prove \(\pi(\partial E)=1\) in the three cases below.

Suppose first that \textup{(i)} holds. By
\Cref{lem:cooperative-critical-extinction}, the CWP converges to \((0,0)\) almost surely and in \(L^1\). For
\(f(x,y):=xy/[(1+x)(1+y)]\), by the convergence and the
definition of the SSP, as $t \rightarrow \infty$, we have
\[
 P_tf(x,y)\rightarrow0,
 \qquad P_t^{\tau_0}f(x,y)\rightarrow0,
 \qquad (x,y)\in E.
\]
By invariance and bounded convergence, every invariant probability
for either realization satisfies \(\pi(f)=0\), and hence
\(\pi(E^\circ)=0\).

Suppose next that \textup{(ii)} holds.
Since \(\theta_i\ge1\), \eqref{eq:cooperative-accessible-noise}
and \cite[Theorem~1.7]{XiongYangZhouEnhancing} give $
 \mathbb P_{x,y}(\tau_0<\infty)>0$ for $(x,y)\in E^\circ.$
The solution in \cite[Theorem~1.7]{XiongYangZhouEnhancing}, stopped at \(\tau_0\), agrees
with both realizations up to that time. Since neither process
can return to \(E^\circ\) after reaching \(\partial E\),
\[
 P_t\1_{E^\circ}(x,y)
 =P_t^{\tau_0}\1_{E^\circ}(x,y)
 =\1_{E^\circ}(x,y)\mathbb P_{x,y}(\tau_0>t).
\]
Thus every invariant probability \(\pi\) satisfies, for \(n\ge1\),
\[
 \pi(E^\circ)
 =\int_{E^\circ}\mathbb P_{x,y}(\tau_0>n)\,\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y),
 \qquad
 \int_{E^\circ}\mathbb P_{x,y}(\tau_0\le n)\,\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)=0.
\]
Letting \(n\to\infty\),
\[
 \int_{E^\circ}\mathbb P_{x,y}(\tau_0<\infty)\,\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)=0,
\]
and hence \(\pi(E^\circ)=0\).

Suppose now that \textup{(iii)} holds. Choose \(c_1,c,C_0\)
as in \Cref{lem:parameter-drift}, set $h=(\theta_1+\kappa_1)\wedge(\theta_2+\kappa_2)$ and 
\begin{equation*}
\beta_i:=\min\bigl\{r_{i1}-2\ \text{if }b_{i1}>0,\;
             r_{i2}-\alpha_i\ \text{if }b_{i2}>0\bigr\},
 \quad i=1,2,\qquad \beta:=\beta_1\vee\beta_2.
\end{equation*}
Fix \(p\in(0,1)\), and set
\begin{align*}
 H_p(x,y):={}&p(1-p)S^{p-2}
       \bigl(b_{11}x^{r_{11}}+c_1^2b_{21}y^{r_{21}}\bigr)\\
 &+\frac{p(1-p)\Gamma(\alpha_1-p)}
        {\Gamma(\alpha_1)\Gamma(2-p)}
       b_{12}x^{r_{12}}S^{p-\alpha_1}
 +\frac{p(1-p)\Gamma(\alpha_2-p)}
        {\Gamma(\alpha_2)\Gamma(2-p)}
       c_1^{\alpha_2}b_{22}y^{r_{22}}S^{p-\alpha_2},
\end{align*}
where $S$ is the function defined by \eqref{SVW}. By \eqref{eq:generator} and
\Cref{lem:cooperative-power-calculus},
\[
 \mathcal L S^p=pS^{p-1}\mathcal L S-H_p(x,y).
\]
 Since \(x\le S\) and \(y\le S/c_1\),
\(\mathcal L S\le CS^h\) for \(0<S\le1\).
The definition of \(\beta_i\) gives constants \(d_1,d_2>0\) such that
\begin{align*}
 H_p(x,y)
 \ge d_1S^{p+\beta_1}\1_{\{x\ge S/2\}}
       +d_2S^{p+\beta_2}\1_{\{c_1y\ge S/2\}}\ge (d_1\wedge d_2)S^{p+\beta},
 \qquad 0<S\le1.
\end{align*}
 Thus, for \(c_*:=d_1\wedge d_2>0\),
\[
 \mathcal L S^p\le CS^{p+h-1}-c_*S^{p+\beta},
 \qquad 0<S\le1.
\]
Since \(\beta<h-1\), choose \(0<\varepsilon\le1\) with
\(C\varepsilon^{h-1-\beta}<c_*\). Then
\(\mathcal L S^p<0\) for \(0<S\le\varepsilon\).
For \(\lambda>0\), let $f_\lambda(s):=1-e^{-\lambda s^p}$ for $s \ge 0$. By \eqref{eq:generator}, one can check that
\[
 \mathcal L f_\lambda(S)
 \le\lambda e^{-\lambda S^p}\mathcal L S^p<0,
 \qquad 0<S\le\varepsilon.
\]
By \eqref{eq:weighted-dissipation}, \(\mathcal L S<0\) for
\(S\ge R\), with some \(R>1\). Since \(f_\lambda\) is increasing and concave,
\[
 \mathcal L f_\lambda(S)
 \le f_\lambda'(S)\mathcal L S<0,\qquad S\ge R.
\]
It remains to consider \(\varepsilon\le S\le R\).
Notice that
\[
 \inf_{\substack{(x,y)\in E\\\varepsilon\le{S(x,y)}\le R}}
 \bigl(b_{11}x^{r_{11}}+c_1^2b_{21}y^{r_{21}}
       +b_{12}x^{r_{12}}+c_1^{\alpha_2}b_{22}y^{r_{22}}\bigr)>0.
\]
Set \(\delta:=p\min_{\varepsilon\le s\le R}s^{p-1}>0\).
Then $
 f_\lambda''(s)/f_\lambda'(s)
 =(p-1)/s-\lambda ps^{p-1}\le-\lambda \delta.$
Moreover,
\[
 0\le\frac{f_\lambda(s+z)-f_\lambda(s)}{f_\lambda'(s)}
 =\frac{1-e^{-\lambda[(s+z)^p-s^p]}}
 {\lambda ps^{p-1}}
 \le\frac1{\lambda \delta},
 \qquad \varepsilon\le s\le R,\quad z>0.
\]
Hence, for \(\lambda \delta>2\), it follows that
\begin{align*}
  \frac1{f_\lambda'(s)}
 \int_0^\infty\bigl[f_\lambda(s+z)-f_\lambda(s)
                    -zf_\lambda'(s)\bigr]\mu_i(\,\mathrm d z) \le-\frac12\int_{2/(\lambda \delta)}^1z\,\mu_i(\,\mathrm d z)
 \le-d_i\lambda^{\alpha_i-1}+C_i.
\end{align*}
Then one can check that $\mathcal L f_\lambda(S) < 0$ for $\varepsilon\le S\le R$, and then $\mathcal L f_\lambda <0$ on $E^\circ$ for large enough $\lambda$.

Let \((Q_t)_{t\ge0}\) be either \((P_t)_{t\ge0}\) or
\((P_t^{\tau_0})_{t\ge0}\), and let \(\pi\) be invariant
for \(Q_t\). Suppose that \(\pi(E^\circ)>0\).
Since \(\partial E\) is absorbing, stationarity gives 
\[
 \pi(\partial E)
 =\pi(\partial E)+\int_{E^\circ}Q_t(z,\partial E)\,\pi(\,\mathrm d z).
\]
It follows that
\[
 \int_{E^\circ}Q_t(z,\partial E)\,\pi(\,\mathrm d z)=0,
 \qquad
 \pi(A)=\int_{E^\circ}Q_t(z,A)\,\pi(\,\mathrm d z),
 \quad A\subset E^\circ.
\]
Consequently, \(\pi_\circ(\cdot):=\pi(\cdot\cap E^\circ)/\pi(E^\circ)\)
is invariant for the process killed upon leaving \(E^\circ\). Started from
\(\pi_\circ\), the process remains in \(E^\circ\): indeed,
\(\mathbb P_{\pi_\circ}(\tau_0\le n)=0\) for every integer \(n\ge1\).
By \eqref{eq:localized-dynkin-inequality} and Fatou's lemma,
using \(0\le f_\lambda\le1\), for \(t>0\), we have
\[
\mathbb E_{\pi_\circ}f_\lambda(S(Z_t)) < \mathbb E_{\pi_\circ}f_\lambda(S(Z_t))
 +\mathbb E_{\pi_\circ}\int_0^t[-\mathcal L(f_\lambda\circ S)](Z_s)\,\mathrm d s
 \le\mathbb E_{\pi_\circ}f_\lambda(S(Z_0)),
\]
which is a contradiction.
Thus \(\pi(E^\circ)=0\), or equivalently, \(\pi(\partial E)=1\), in all three cases.
By \Cref{def:absorbed}, every probability concentrated on
\(\partial E\) is invariant for the SSP.
For the CWP, similar to the axis argument in the proof of
\Cref{prop:noimm-classification}\textup{(ii)}, with
\(b_{10},b_{20}>0\), it gives \(\pi=\delta_{(0,0)}\).

label: eqmcA
title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{q1q2}, we have $
	\Psi_1(\widehat q_1)<a_2\widehat q_2$ and
	$\Psi_2(\widehat q_2)<a_1\widehat q_1.$
	Choose $
	0<\delta<\frac14\min\bigl\{
	a_2\widehat q_2-\Psi_1(\widehat q_1),\,
	a_1\widehat q_1-\Psi_2(\widehat q_2)\bigr\}.$
	Using the cutoff \(\chi\)
	fixed at the beginning of
		\Cref{sec:cooperative-noimm-proofs}, we set
	\[
	g_i(u)=1+\varepsilon_i\chi(u)u^{-\widehat q_i},
	\qquad F(x,y)=g_1(x)g_2(y),
	\]
	where \(\varepsilon_i>0\) will be chosen below. Let
	\begin{eqnarray}\label{eqmcA}
	\mathcal A_i g(u):= -b_{i0}u^{r_{i0}}g'(u)
	+b_{i1}u^3g''(u) +b_{i2}u^{\alpha_i+1}
	\int_0^\infty
	[g(u+z)-g(u)-zg'(u)]\,\mu_i(\,\mathrm d z).
	\end{eqnarray}
	For \(0<u\le1\), \Cref{lem:cooperative-power-calculus} and
	\(g_i(u+z)\le1+\varepsilon_i(u+z)^{-\widehat q_i}\)
	give {
		\[
		\begin{aligned}
			\frac{\mathcal A_i g_i(u)}{g_i(u)}
			\le\frac{\varepsilon_i\Psi_i(\widehat q_i)u
				+\widehat q_i b_{i0}\varepsilon_i u^{r_{i0}-1}}
			{u^{\widehat q_i}+\varepsilon_i}
			\le\Psi_i(\widehat q_i)u
			+\frac{\widehat q_i b_{i0}\varepsilon_i u^{r_{i0}-1}}
			{u^{\widehat q_i}+\varepsilon_i}.
		\end{aligned}
		\]
		Since \(r_{i0}>2\),
		\[
		\lim_{\varepsilon_i\downarrow0}\sup_{0<u\le1}
		\frac{\varepsilon_i u^{r_{i0}-2}}
		{u^{\widehat q_i}+\varepsilon_i}=0.
		\]
		On \([1,2]\), the three terms on the right hand of
		\eqref{eqmcA} are \(O(\varepsilon_i)\).
		For \(u\ge2\), all those terms vanish. We may therefore fix
		\(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2>0\) sufficiently small that
		\[
		\frac{\mathcal A_i g_i(u)}{g_i(u)}
		\le[\Psi_i(\widehat q_i)+\delta]u,
		\qquad u>0,\quad i=1,2
		\]
		for constant $
		0<\delta<\frac14\min\{
		a_2\widehat q_2-\Psi_1(\widehat q_1),\,
		a_1\widehat q_1-\Psi_2(\widehat q_2)\}.$
		Let $
		h_i(u)=-\frac{ug_i'(u)}{g_i(u)}\ge0.$
		Then \(h_i(u)\to\widehat q_i\) as \(u\downarrow0\), and
		\eqref{eq:generator} gives
		\begin{align*}
			\frac{\mathcal L F(x,y)}{F(x,y)}
			&=\frac{\mathcal A_1g_1(x)}{g_1(x)}
			+\frac{\mathcal A_2g_2(y)}{g_2(y)}
			-a_2xh_2(y)-a_1yh_1(x)\\
			&\le[\Psi_1(\widehat q_1)+\delta-a_2h_2(y)]x
			+[\Psi_2(\widehat q_2)+\delta-a_1h_1(x)]y.
		\end{align*}
		Choose \(r\in(0,1)\) so that the first bracket is at most
		\(-\tilde\delta\) for all \(y\le r\) and some
		$\tilde\delta>0$, and the second is at most
		\(-\tilde\delta\) for all \(x\le r\). Next choose
		\[
		0<\eta\le r\min\left\{1,\,
		\frac{\tilde\delta/2}{\Psi_1(\widehat q_1)+\delta},\,
		\frac{\tilde\delta/2}{\Psi_2(\widehat q_2)+\delta}\right\}.
		\]
		If \(x,y\le r\), then
		$\mathcal L F(x,y)/F(x,y)$ is at most
		\(-\tilde\delta(x+y)\).
		If \(x\ge r\) and \(y\le\eta\), we have
		\[
		\frac{\mathcal L F(x,y)}{F(x,y)}
		\le-\tilde\delta x+
		[\Psi_2(\widehat q_2)+ \delta]y
		\le-\frac{\tilde\delta x}{2}
		\le-\frac{\tilde\delta}{4}(x+y).
		\]
		Interchanging the coordinates treats
		\(y\ge r\) and \(x\le\eta\).
		Hence $
		\mathcal L F\le-\frac{\tilde\delta}{4}SF$
		when $x\wedge y\le\eta.$
		On \(\{x\wedge y>\eta\}\), \(F\) is bounded and
		\(\mathcal L F\le C_\eta S\), which yields $
		\mathcal L F\le-\frac{\tilde\delta}{4}SF+C_\eta S$
		on \(E^\circ\).
		By \Cref{lem:parameter-drift},
		\(\mathcal L S\le C_0-c_0W_0\) with \(c_1=1\).
		Thus
		\(\mathcal L V\le C-cW\).
		At infinity, \(S\) controls \(V\) and \(W_0\) controls \(W\).
		Away from the origin, both \(F\) and \(SF\) diverge on
		approach to either axis. As $(x,y)\rightarrow(0,0)$,
		\[
		SF\ge\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2
		(x+y)x^{-\widehat q_1}y^{-\widehat q_2}
		\ge\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2
		(x+y)^{1-\widehat q_1-\widehat q_2}\rightarrow\infty.
		\]
		Also $\lim_{x,y\rightarrow0}F(x,y)=\infty$.}
	Thus \(V\) and \(W\) have compact sublevel sets
	in \(E^\circ\).

	by the concavity of \(\phi_n\), \eqref{eq:generator}, \eqref{eq1007} and \eqref{eq:sharp-R-generator}, we have
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		0&\le\phi_n'(R)\mathcal L R-\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ R)\\
		&\le-\phi_n''(R)
		\left(\frac{b_{11}}x+\frac{b_{21}}y\right)
		+\frac{C}{R}\1_{\{R\ge n\}}
		\Bigg[
		b_{12}x^{\alpha_1+1}
		\int_0^\infty \left(\frac1x-\frac1{x+z}\right)^2\,\mu_1(\,\mathrm d z)\cr 
		&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad  +b_{22}y^{\alpha_2+1}
		\int_0^\infty \left(\frac1y-\frac1{y+z}\right)^2\,\mu_2(\,\mathrm d z)
		\Bigg].
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	The substitutions \(z=xt\), respectively, yield
	\[
	x^{\alpha_i+1}\int_0^\infty \left(\frac1x-\frac1{x+z}\right)^2\,\mu_i(\,\mathrm d z)
	=\frac{\alpha_i(\alpha_i-1)}x.
	\]
	Moreover, since \(\|\phi_n''\|_\infty\le C/n\) and
	\(\phi_n''=0\) on \([n,2n]^c\),
	\[
	0\le-\phi_n''(R)
	\left(\frac{b_{11}}x+\frac{b_{21}}y\right)
	\le\frac{CR}{n}\1_{\{n\le R\le2n\}}
	\le C\1_{\{R\ge n\}}.
	\]
	Combining these estimates with \(x^{-1}+y^{-1}=R\), we obtain
	\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq1006b}
	0\le\phi_n'(R(x,y))\mathcal L R(x,y)
	-\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ R)(x,y)
	\le C\1_{\{R(x,y)\ge n\}}.
	\end{eqnarray}
	For fixed \(n\), by \(\phi_n'(R(x,y))R(x,y)\le2n\), we have $
	\phi_n'(R(x,y))\frac{y}{x}\le2ny$ and $
	\phi_n'(R(x,y))\frac{x}{y}\le2nx.$
	Using \(r_{10},r_{20}>2\) and
	\eqref{eq:sharp-R-generator}, we obtain
	\[
	|\phi_n'(R(x,y))\mathcal L R(x,y)|
	\le C_n(1+W_0(x,y)).
	\]
	Hence by the above and \eqref{eq1006b},
	\begin{eqnarray*}
	|\mathcal L (\phi_n\circ R(x, y))| \le |\phi_n'(R(x, y))\mathcal L R(x, y)| + C\1_{\{R(x,y)\ge n\}} \le C_n(1+W_0(x,y)) + C.
	\end{eqnarray*}
It follows that \(\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ R)\in L^1(\pi)\).
	As in \eqref{eq:localized-dynkin-martingale}, by It\^o's
	formula,
	\begin{eqnarray}\label{Mt} 
	M_t^{n,R}:=\phi_n(R(Z_t))-\phi_n(R(Z_0))
	-\int_0^t\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ R)(Z_s)\,\mathrm d s 
	\end{eqnarray} 
	is a local martingale. 
	For every \(T>0\), 
	\[
	\sup_{0\le t\le T}|M_t^{n,R}|
	\le2\|\phi_n\|_\infty
	+\int_0^T|\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ R)(Z_s)|\,\mathrm d s.
	\]
	Under \(\mathbb P_\pi\), \(Z_s\) has distribution \(\pi\) for every
	\(s\ge0\). Hence,  
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		\mathbb E_\pi\int_0^T
		|\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ R)(Z_s)|\,\mathrm d s
	  =T\int_{E^\circ}
		|\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ R)(z)|\,\pi(\,\mathrm d z)
		<\infty.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
  Thus localization and dominated
	convergence show that \(M^{n,R}\) is a martingale.
	Taking stationary expectations to \eqref{Mt}, we have
	\begin{equation}
		0=\mathbb E_\pi[\phi_n(R(Z_t))-\phi_n(R(Z_0))]
		=t\int_{E^\circ}\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ R)(x,y)
		\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y),\qquad t>0.
		\label{eq:sharp-R-stationarity}
	\end{equation}
	Consequently, by \eqref{eq:sharp-R-generator},
	\eqref{eq:sharp-R-stationarity}, and the nonnegative
	generator difference above,
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		\int_{E^\circ}\phi_n'(R(x,y))
		\left(a_1\frac{y}{x}+a_2\frac{x}{y}\right)\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)
		&\le\Psi_1(1)+\Psi_2(1)\\
		&\quad+\int_{E^\circ}
		(b_{10}x^{r_{10}-2}+b_{20}y^{r_{20}-2})
		\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y).
	\end{aligned}
	\] }
	Letting \(n\to\infty\), the first assertion follows
	from Fatou's lemma.
	
	Now fix \(p,q>0\) with \(p+q=1\), and set
		\(f(x,y)=x^{-p}y^{-q}\). By \eqref{eq:generator},
	\[
	\frac{\mathcal L f(x,y)}{f(x,y)}
	=[\Psi_1(p)-a_2q]x+[\Psi_2(q)-a_1p]y
	+p b_{10}x^{r_{10}-1}+q b_{20}y^{r_{20}-1}.
	\]
	Since \(xf(x,y)=(x/y)^q\) and \(yf(x,y)=(y/x)^p\),
	the first assertion gives $
	\int_{E^\circ}(xf(x,y)+yf(x,y))\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)<\infty.$ 
Similar to \eqref{eq1006b}, one can check that
\[
0\le \phi_n'(f)\mathcal L f-\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ f)
\le C(xf+yf)\1_{\{f\ge n\}} 
\]
and \(\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ f)\in L^1(\pi)\).
Repeating the argument leading to
\eqref{eq:sharp-R-stationarity}, we obtain $
\int_{E^\circ}\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ f)(x, y)\,\pi(\,\mathrm d x, \,\mathrm d y)=0.$
Consequently,
\begin{eqnarray}
	\label{eq:sharp-truncated-f-identity}
		0
		\!\!\!&\le\!\!\!& \int_{E^\circ}\phi_n'(f(x, y))\mathcal L f(x, y)\,\pi(\,\mathrm d x, \,\mathrm d y) =\int_{E^\circ}
		[\phi_n'(f(x, y))\mathcal L f(x, y)-\mathcal L(\phi_n\circ f)(x, y)]\,\pi(\,\mathrm d x, \,\mathrm d y)\cr
		\!\!\!&\le\!\!\!& C\int_{E^\circ}(xf(x, y)+yf(x, y))
		\1_{\{f(x, y)\ge n\}}\,\pi(\,\mathrm d x, \,\mathrm d y).
	\end{eqnarray}
	The right-hand side of \eqref{eq:sharp-truncated-f-identity} tends to zero as \(n\to\infty\)
	by dominated convergence.
	The nonnegative self-regulation terms in \(\mathcal L f\) imply $
	(\mathcal L f)^-(x,y)\le C(xf(x,y)+yf(x,y)),$
	so \((\mathcal L f)^-\in L^1(\pi)\). Hence, as \(n\to\infty\),
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		\int_{E^\circ}\phi_n'(f(x,y))(\mathcal L f)^+(x,y)
		\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)
		&=\int_{E^\circ}\phi_n'(f(x,y))\mathcal L f(x,y)
		\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)\\
		&\quad+\int_{E^\circ}\phi_n'(f(x,y))(\mathcal L f)^-(x,y)
		\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)\\
		&\longrightarrow\int_{E^\circ}(\mathcal L f)^-(x,y)
		\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y).
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	Fatou's lemma gives \((\mathcal L f)^+\in L^1(\pi)\), and hence
	\(\mathcal L f\in L^1(\pi)\). Letting \(n\to\infty\) in
	\eqref{eq:sharp-truncated-f-identity} and applying dominated
	convergence, we obtain $
	\int_{E^\circ}\mathcal L f(x,y)\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)=0.$
	The result follows.

label: eq:imm-uniform-exit
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(t>0\) and let \((x_n,y_n)\to(x_0,y_0)\) in \(E\).
On one probability space, use \(B_1,B_2,N_1,N_2\) to construct
the solutions \((X^{(n)},Y^{(n)})\) and \(Z\) with these
initial states. For \(R>1\), let
\[
 \rho_R^{(n)}:=\inf\{s\ge0:
 X_s^{(n)}\vee Y_s^{(n)}\vee X_s\vee Y_s\ge R\}.
\]
By convergence of the initial states,
\Cref{lem:imm-lyapunov} gives
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{n\ge1}
 \mathbb P(\rho_R^{(n)}\le t)=0.
 \label{eq:imm-uniform-exit}
\end{equation}
For fixed \(R\), \eqref{eq:stopped-L1-continuity} in
\Cref{prop:imm-wellposed} yields
\[
 \mathbb E\bigl[|X_{t\wedge\rho_R^{(n)}}^{(n)}-X_{t\wedge\rho_R^{(n)}}|
 +|Y_{t\wedge\rho_R^{(n)}}^{(n)}-Y_{t\wedge\rho_R^{(n)}}|\bigr]
 \le\mathrm e^{C_Rt}(|x_n-x_0|+|y_n-y_0|),
\]
{ which gives}
\[
 |X_{t\wedge\rho_R^{(n)}}^{(n)}-X_{t\wedge\rho_R^{(n)}}|
 +|Y_{t\wedge\rho_R^{(n)}}^{(n)}-Y_{t\wedge\rho_R^{(n)}}|
 \rightarrow0
\]
{in probability as \(n\to\infty\).
For \(f\in C_b(E)\), we have}
\[
 \mathbb E\left[
 \left|f(X_t^{(n)},Y_t^{(n)})-f(Z_t)\right|
 \1_{\{\rho_R^{(n)}>t\}}
 \right]\rightarrow0\quad{\text{as }n\to\infty}.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{align*}
 &\left|P_tf(x_n,y_n)-P_tf({x_0,y_0})\right|\\
 &\quad\le
 \mathbb E\left[
 \left|f(X_t^{(n)},Y_t^{(n)})-f(Z_t)\right|
 \1_{\{\rho_R^{(n)}>t\}}
 \right]
 +2\lVert f\rVert_\infty\mathbb P(\rho_R^{(n)}\le t).
\end{align*}
Taking first \(n\to\infty\) and then \(R\to\infty\),
and using \eqref{eq:imm-uniform-exit}, we obtain
\(P_tf(x_n,y_n)\to P_tf(x_0,y_0)\).
Thus \(P_tf\in C_b(E)\). The result follows.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:imm-time-averages}
For every \((x_0,y_0)\in E\), the family
\(\{\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}:T\ge1\}\) is tight, and every weak
limit as \(T\to\infty\) is an invariant probability.

title: Proof
body_md:
Nonexplosion and conservativeness follow from
\Cref{lem:imm-lyapunov}, while \Cref{lem:imm-weak-feller} gives the
weak Feller property.  {By \Cref{lem:imm-lyapunov} again,
there exists a constant \(C>0\) such that, for \(T\ge1\),}
\[
 \int_E {V_0}(u,v)\,\Pi_T^{({x_0,y_0})}(\,\mathrm d u,\,\mathrm d v)
 =\frac1T\int_0^T\mathbb E_{{x_0,y_0}}{V_0}(Z_t)\,\mathrm d t
 \le\frac{{V_0}({x_0,y_0})}{T}+C.
\]
Markov's inequality therefore yields
\[
 \sup_{T\ge1}\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}({V_0}>R)
 \le \frac{{V_0}(x_0,y_0)+C}{R}
 \rightarrow0\qquad\text{as }R\to\infty.
\]
Each set \(\{V_0\le R\}\) is compact in \(E\). Hence
\(\{\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}:T\ge1\}\) is tight.
The invariance of every weak limit as \(T\to\infty\)
follows from \Cref{lem:time-average-limits}.

title: Proof

Since \(u^q\le1+u^r\) for \(u\ge0\) and \(0\le q\le r\), by
stationarity, \eqref{eq:imm-moment} and
\eqref{eq:noise-moment-order}, we have, for \(j=1,2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_\pi\int_0^t
 \bigl(b_{1j}X_s^{r_{1j}}+b_{2j}Y_s^{r_{2j}}\bigr)\,\mathrm d s=t\int_E
 \bigl(b_{1j}x^{r_{1j}}+b_{2j}y^{r_{2j}}\bigr)\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)
 <\infty.
\end{aligned}
\]
Split each stable integral at \(z=1\). By It\^o's isometry,
the Brownian and compensated small-jump terms of $M_t$ are square-integrable
martingales. Since \(\int_1^\infty z\,\mu_i(\,\mathrm d z)<\infty\),
the preceding bound also makes each compensated large-jump term of $M_t$
are integrable martingale. Thus \((M_t)_{t \ge 0}\) is an integrable martingale
with \(\mathbb E_\pi M_t=0\).

body_md:
For \(t<\tau_N^+\), we have $X_t^{r_{10}}\le N^{r_{10}-1}X_t,$
and hence the first drift in \eqref{eq:sqrt-system} is bounded below by
\(\iota_1-c_{1,N}X_t\).  For \(0\le v\le N\), set {$h_N(v):=(-a_2)N^{\kappa_2}v^{\kappa_1}+b_{20}v^{r_{20}}.$}

and set $c_{2,N}:=\max_{\delta_N\le v\le N}\frac{h_N(v)}{v}.$

\(\iota_2/2-c_{2,N}Y_t\) before \(\tau_N^+\). Moreover, \eqref{eq:cir-localized-comparison} follows by the comparison theorem, see, e.g.,

 \le N^{\kappa_1+\kappa_2-1}v$ and $v^{r_{20}}\le N^{r_{20}-1}v.$

In the case \(a_1>0>a_2\), under \eqref{eq:balanced-interactions},
\eqref{eq:cir-localized-comparison} and \eqref{eq:CIR-no-atom} give
\[
 \mathbb P(X_t=0,\ \tau_N^+>t)
 \le\mathbb P(U_t^{(1,N)}=0)=0,
\]
and the same argument applies to \(Y_t\).
When \(\theta_i\ge1\), \(i=1,2\), these estimates follow
instead from \eqref{eq:cir-generalized-comparison}, using
\(V^{(1,N)}\) and \(V^{(2,N)}\).
Thus, in either case,
\[
 \mathbb P(X_t=0\text{ or }Y_t=0)\le\mathbb P(\tau_N^+\le t).
\]
Since the solution is nonexplosive, \(\lim_{N\to\infty}\tau_N^+=\infty\)
almost surely. Letting \(N\to\infty\) proves
\eqref{eq:fixed-time-interior}.

\textup{(ii)} In the case \(a_1>0>a_2\), use the lower
processes \(U^{(1,N)}\) and \(\widetilde U^{(2,N)}\) from
\eqref{eq:cir-localized-comparison} and
\eqref{eq:cir-strengthened-comparison}.
When \(\theta_i\ge1\), \(i=1,2\), use
\(V^{(1,N)}\) and \(V^{(2,N)}\) from
\eqref{eq:cir-generalized-comparison}.
In both cases, the lower CIR processes have immigration
rates \(\iota_i\) and diffusion coefficients
\(v\mapsto\sqrt{2b_{i1}v}\).
By \eqref{eq:Feller-thresholds} and \eqref{eq:CIR-pathwise-positive},
they remain positive at every positive time almost surely.
The corresponding comparisons therefore give
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb P(X_t>0,Y_t>0\text{ for every }0<t<\tau_N^+)=1.
\end{equation*}
Letting \(N\to\infty\) and using nonexplosion proves
\eqref{eq:pathwise-interior}.

\(i=1,2\), \Cref{prop:sqrt-boundary}\textup{(ii)} implies that
\(E^\circ\) is invariant.
  Fix

\((x_n,y_n)\to({x_0,y_0})\) in \(E^\circ\).
Let \((X^{(n)},Y^{(n)})\) and \(Z\) solve
\eqref{eq:sqrt-system} with initial states \((x_n,y_n)\) and
\((x_0,y_0)\), respectively.
Let \((D_m)_{m\ge1}\) be a sequence of bounded smooth domains such that
\(D_m\Subset D_{m+1}\Subset E^\circ\) and
\(\bigcup_{m\ge1}D_m=E^\circ\).
{By Proposition \ref{prop:sqrt-boundary} and
nonexplosion, the exit times \(\tau_m:=\tau_{D_m}^{(x_0,y_0)}\)
satisfy \(\tau_m\uparrow\infty\) almost surely as $m \rightarrow \infty$. Fix \(\varepsilon>0\). Choose \(m\) large
enough such that \((x_0,y_0)\in D_m\) and}
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{{x_0,y_0}}(\tau_m\le t)<\varepsilon.
 \label{eq:exit-xy-small}
\end{equation}
Choose a bounded smooth domain \(D'\) with
\(\overline D_m\subset D'\Subset E^\circ\).
Choose a smooth function \(\chi\) with compact support in \(E^\circ\),
\(0\le\chi\le1\), and \(\chi=1\) on a neighborhood of
\(\overline{D'}\).  Set
\[
 \widetilde b:=\chi b,
 \qquad \widetilde\sigma:=\chi\sigma+(1-\chi)I_2
 \quad\text{on }E^\circ,
\]
and extend these coefficients by \(0\) and \(I_2\), respectively,
outside \(E^\circ\), where \(I_2\) is the \(2\times2\) identity 
matrix. Then \(\widetilde b,\widetilde\sigma\in C_b^\infty(\mathbb R^2)\),
and they agree with \(b,\sigma\) near \(\overline{D'}\).
  Since \(\sigma\) is
diagonal with positive entries on the compact support of \(\chi\),
there is a constant \(\lambda>0\) such that
\[
 \widetilde\sigma(w)\widetilde\sigma(w)^\top\ge\lambda I_2,
 \qquad w\in\mathbb R^2.
\]
For an initial state \((u,v)\in\mathbb R^2\), let
\((\widetilde X,\widetilde Y)\) solve
{
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \begin{pmatrix}\widetilde X_t\\\widetilde Y_t\end{pmatrix}
 = \begin{pmatrix}u\\v\end{pmatrix}
 +\int_0^t\widetilde b(\widetilde X_s,\widetilde Y_s)\,\mathrm d s +\int_0^t\widetilde\sigma(\widetilde X_s,\widetilde Y_s)
 \begin{pmatrix}\,\mathrm d B_1(s)\\\,\mathrm d B_2(s)\end{pmatrix},
\end{aligned}
 \label{eq:sqrt-modified-system}
\end{equation}
and denote its}
transition semigroup by \((\widetilde P_t)_{t\ge0}\).
  Then by the smoothness, boundedness, and uniform
ellipticity of these coefficients, one sees that
$\widetilde P_t$ maps $B_b(\mathbb R^2)$ to $C_b(\mathbb R^2)$ for every \(t>0\), see
\cite[Theorem~7.2.4]{StroockVaradhan2006}.
 

Choose a smooth domain \(D''\) with
\(\overline D_m\subset D''\Subset D'\).
{The coefficients are Lipschitz on \(\overline{D'}\).
By the Burkholder--Davis--Gundy inequality and Gronwall's
inequality, one obtains}
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\sup_{0\le s\le t\wedge\tau_{D'}^{(x_n,y_n)}
                         \wedge\tau_{D'}^{({x_0,y_0})}}
 \bigl|(X_s^{(n)},Y_s^{(n)})-Z_s\bigr|^2
 \le C_{D',t}\bigl|(x_n,y_n)-({x_0,y_0})\bigr|^2,
 \label{eq:interior-flow-stability}
\end{equation}
{where \(C_{D',t}>0\) is independent of \(n\).}
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \((x_n,y_n)\in D_m\).
On the event
\(\{\tau_{D'}^{(x_n,y_n)}\le t<\tau_{D''}^{({x_0,y_0})}\}\),
set \(s:=\tau_{D'}^{(x_n,y_n)}\).
Then \(s\le t<\tau_{D''}^{({x_0,y_0})}
\le\tau_{D'}^{({x_0,y_0})}\), since \(D''\subset D'\), and hence
\(s=t\wedge\tau_{D'}^{(x_n,y_n)}
\wedge\tau_{D'}^{({x_0,y_0})}\).
By continuity of the sample paths,
\[
 (X_s^{(n)},Y_s^{(n)})\in\partial D',
 \qquad Z_s\in D''.
\]
Therefore, on \(\{\tau_{D'}^{(x_n,y_n)}\le t<
\tau_{D''}^{(x_0,y_0)}\}\),
\begin{eqnarray*}
 \sup_{0\le r\le t\wedge\tau_{D'}^{(x_n,y_n)}
                        \wedge\tau_{D'}^{(x_0,y_0)}}
 \bigl|(X_r^{(n)},Y_r^{(n)})-(X_r,Y_r)\bigr|
 \ge\bigl|(X_s^{(n)},Y_s^{(n)})-Z_s\bigr| \ge d,
\end{eqnarray*}
where \(d:=\operatorname{dist}(\overline{D''},\partial D')>0\).
Consequently, by Markov's inequality
 and
\eqref{eq:interior-flow-stability}, for all sufficiently large
\(n\), we have
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{x_n,y_n}(\tau_{D'}\le t)
 \le\mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(\tau_{D''}\le t)
 +\frac{C_{D',t}}{d^2}|(x_n,y_n)-(x_0,y_0)|^2.
 \label{eq:nearby-exit-bound}
\end{equation}
Since \(D_m\subset D''\subset D'\), \eqref{eq:exit-xy-small} yields
\[
 \mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(\tau_{D'}\le t)
 \le\mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(\tau_{D''}\le t)
 \le\mathbb P_{x_0,y_0}(\tau_m\le t)<\varepsilon.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:nearby-exit-bound}, this implies, for all
sufficiently large \(n\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{x_n,y_n}(\tau_{D'}\le t)<2\varepsilon.
 \label{eq:nearby-exit-small}
\end{equation}
Let \(f\in B_b(E^\circ)\) and extend it to a bounded Borel function
\(\widetilde f\) on \(\mathbb R^2\) with the same supremum norm.
For a common initial state \((u,v)\in D'\), the solutions of
\eqref{eq:sqrt-system} and \eqref{eq:sqrt-modified-system} satisfy
\[
 Z_s=(\widetilde X_s,\widetilde Y_s),
 \qquad 0\le s\le\tau_{D'},
\]
by pathwise uniqueness and continuity, since
\(b=\widetilde b\) and \(\sigma=\widetilde\sigma\) on \(D'\).
Recall that \(\widetilde f=f\) on \(E^\circ\) and
\(\|\widetilde f\|_\infty=\|f\|_\infty\).
Thus, on \(\{\tau_{D'}\ge t\}\),
\(f(Z_t)=\widetilde f(\widetilde X_t,\widetilde Y_t)\).
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 |P_tf(u,v)-\widetilde P_t\widetilde f(u,v)|
 &=\left|\mathbb E_{u,v}\left[
 \bigl(f(Z_t)-\widetilde f(\widetilde X_t,\widetilde Y_t)\bigr)
 \1_{\{\tau_{D'}<t\}}\right]\right|\\
 &\le2\|f\|_\infty\,\mathbb P_{u,v}(\tau_{D'}\le t).
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:localized-semigroup-bound}
\end{equation}
Since \(\widetilde P_t\widetilde f\in C_b(\mathbb R^2)\),
\begin{align*}
  |P_tf(x_n,y_n)-P_tf(x_0,y_0)|&\le |P_tf(x_n,y_n)-\widetilde P_t\widetilde f(x_n,y_n)|\\
 &\quad+|\widetilde P_t\widetilde f(x_n,y_n)
            -\widetilde P_t\widetilde f(x_0,y_0)| +|\widetilde P_t\widetilde f(x_0,y_0)-P_tf(x_0,y_0)|.
\end{align*}
The middle term tends to zero as \(n\to\infty\). By
\eqref{eq:exit-xy-small}, \eqref{eq:nearby-exit-small}, and
\eqref{eq:localized-semigroup-bound}, the first and last terms
are bounded by \(4\varepsilon\|f\|_\infty\) and
\(2\varepsilon\|f\|_\infty\), respectively, for all sufficiently
large \(n\). Hence
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}|P_tf(x_n,y_n)-P_tf(x_0,y_0)|
 \le6\varepsilon\lVert f\rVert_\infty.
\]
Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) proves the assertion.

label: eq:support-control
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(({x_0,y_0})\in E^\circ\), a nonempty open set
\(O\subset E^\circ\), and \(t>0\).
Choose \(q\in O\) and set
\[
 \phi(s):=\left(1-\frac{s}{t}\right)(x_0,y_0)
             +\frac{s}{t}q,\qquad 0\le s\le t.
\]
Define
\[
b^{\mathrm S}(x,y)
:=b(x,y)-\frac12\begin{pmatrix}b_{11}\\b_{21}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since \(b_{11},b_{21}>0\), the matrix \(\sigma(x,y)\)
is invertible on \(E^\circ\). Define
\begin{equation}
 u(s):=\sigma(\phi(s))^{-1}
       \bigl(\dot\phi(s)-b^{\mathrm S}(\phi(s))\bigr) 
 \label{eq:support-control}
\end{equation}
By compactness, there exist \(0<\varepsilon<N<\infty\) such that
\(\phi([0,t])\subset[\varepsilon,N]^2\).
The inverse of \(\sigma\) is continuous and bounded on
\([\varepsilon,N]^2\).
  Moreover, both \(\dot\phi\) and
\(b^{\mathrm S}\circ\phi\) are continuous and bounded on \([0,t]\).
Hence \(u\) is bounded, and therefore
\[
 \int_0^t |u(s)|^2\,\mathrm d s
 \le t\sup_{0\le s\le t}|u(s)|^2<\infty.
\]
 By \eqref{eq:support-control}, 
\[
 {\dot\phi(s)
 =b^{\mathrm S}(\phi(s))+\sigma(\phi(s))u(s),
 \qquad 0\le s\le t.}
\]
Choose a bounded domain \(D\) with smooth boundary such that
\(\phi([0,t])\subset D\Subset E^\circ\).
As in the proof of \Cref{lem:sqrt-interior-strong-feller},
construct coefficients \(\widetilde b,\widetilde\sigma\in
C_b^\infty(\mathbb R^2)\), with uniformly elliptic covariance,
that agree with \(b,\sigma\) near \(\overline D\).
Let \(\widetilde Z := (\widetilde X,\widetilde Y)\) denote the solution to 
\eqref{eq:sqrt-modified-system} with 
initial state \((x_0,y_0)\), and the Brownian motions
\(B_1,B_2\) driving \(Z\).
Choose \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
 \delta<\operatorname{dist}\bigl(\phi([0,t]),\mathbb R^2\setminus D\bigr),
 \qquad B(q,\delta)\subset O.
\]
The path \(\phi\) satisfies the controlled equation for the
extended coefficients as well. Thus the support theorem
\cite[Theorem~3.5]{MilletSanzSole1994}, applied with
\(h(s):=\int_0^s u(r)\,\mathrm d r\) and a deterministic rescaling
of \([0,t]\) to \([0,1]\), gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{{x_0,y_0}}\left(
 \sup_{0\le s\le t}
 |(\widetilde X_s,\widetilde Y_s)-\phi(s)|<\delta
 \right)>0.
 \label{eq:support-event}
\end{equation}
On the event in \eqref{eq:support-event},
\(\widetilde Z_s\in B(\phi(s),\delta)\subset D\)
for every \(0\le s\le t\). Since the coefficients agree on \(D\), local pathwise uniqueness
gives \(Z_s= \widetilde Z_s\) for all
\(s\in[0,t]\) on this event. In particular,
\[
 Z_t= \widetilde Z_t 
 \in B(\phi(t),\delta)=B(q,\delta)\subset O.
\]
The event in \eqref{eq:support-event} has positive probability.
Hence \(P_t((x_0,y_0),O)>0\).

title: Proof
body_md:
\textup{(i)}
The square-root model \eqref{eq:sqrt-system} is the special case of
\eqref{eq:model} with \(r_{11}=r_{21}=1\) and \(b_{12}=b_{22}=0\).
Existence and the moment bounds follow from
\Cref{thm:imm-existence}. Since
\(r_{11}=r_{21}=1<r_{i0}\), \(i=1,2\),
\eqref{eq:stationary-balance} follows by \Cref{cor:stationary-balance}.
To prove the remaining assertions, let \(\pi\) be
any invariant probability and fix \(t>0\).
By \Cref{prop:sqrt-boundary}\textup{(i)},
\(P_t((x_0,y_0),E^\circ)=1\) for every
\((x_0,y_0)\in E\). Consequently,
\[
 \pi(E^\circ)
 =\int_EP_t((x,y),E^\circ)\pi(\,\mathrm d x,\,\mathrm d y)=1.
\]
Let \(G=E\cap O\ne\varnothing\), where \(O\) is open in \(\mathbb R^2\).
Since \(E^\circ\) is dense in \(E\), \(G\cap E^\circ\) is a nonempty open
subset of \(E^\circ\). Recall that \(\pi(E^\circ)=1\). By
\Cref{lem:sqrt-interior-irreducibility},
\[
 \pi(G)\ge\pi(G\cap E^\circ)
 =\int_{E^\circ}P_t((u,v),G\cap E^\circ)\pi(\,\mathrm d u,\,\mathrm d v)>0
\]
for any \(t>0\). Since \(G\) was arbitrary, we conclude that
\(\operatorname{supp}\pi=E\).


 \textup{(ii)}
We first prove uniqueness. Existence follows from \textup{(i)}.
Let \(\pi_1\) and \(\pi_2\) be invariant probabilities on \(E\).
By \textup{(i)}, both assign mass one to \(E^\circ\).
Since \(E^\circ\) is invariant by
\Cref{lem:sqrt-interior-strong-feller}, both probabilities are
invariant for the restricted semigroup on \(E^\circ\).
The restricted semigroup is strong Feller by
\Cref{lem:sqrt-interior-strong-feller}. It is also irreducible:
\Cref{lem:sqrt-interior-irreducibility} gives
\(P_t(z,O)>0\) for every \(t>0\), \(z\in E^\circ\),
and nonempty open \(O\subset E^\circ\). Thus every
\(P_t(z,\cdot)\) has full support in \(E^\circ\).
To apply Doob's uniqueness theorem, we show that, for each
\(t>0\), the measures \(P_{2t}(z,\cdot)\), \(z\in E^\circ\),
are mutually absolutely continuous. Fix a Borel set
\(A\subset E^\circ\). If
\(P_{2t}((x,y),A)=0\) for some \((x,y)\in E^\circ\), then
\[
 0=\int_{E^\circ}P_t((u,v),A)\,P_t((x,y),\,\mathrm d u,\,\mathrm d v).
\]
The integrand is continuous and nonnegative by the strong Feller
property, while \(P_t((x,y),\cdot)\) has full support on
\(E^\circ\). Hence \(P_t((u,v),A)=0\) for every
\((u,v)\in E^\circ\). It follows that all the measures
\(P_{2t}((u,v),\cdot)\), \((u,v)\in E^\circ\), are
equivalent. By \cite[Theorem~1, p.~84]{KulikScheutzow2015},
the chain obtained by observing the process at times
\(0,2t,4t,\ldots\) has at most one invariant probability.
Both \(\pi_1\) and \(\pi_2\) are invariant for this chain,
so \(\pi_1=\pi_2\).


We next prove convergence of the time-averaged transition laws.
Let \(\pi\) be the unique invariant probability.
By \Cref{lem:imm-time-averages}, the family
\(\{\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}:T\ge1\}\) is tight, and every weak
subsequential limit is invariant. Hence every such limit equals
\(\pi\), and \(\Pi_T^{(x_0,y_0)}\Rightarrow\pi\) as
\(T\to\infty\).

title: Proof
body_md:
First suppose that \((x_0,y_0)\in E^\circ\). For all sufficiently
	large integers \(n\), let
	\(p_n(u):=(u\vee n^{-1})\wedge n\) and
	\(D_n:=(n^{-1},n)^2\).
	Replace each state variable \(u\) in \eqref{eq:model} by
	\(p_n(u)\). The truncated drift is bounded and Lipschitz. Moreover, for \(u,v\in\mathbb R\) and \(i=1,2\), we have
	\(b_{i2}|p_n(u)^{r_{i2}}-p_n(v)^{r_{i2}}|
	\le C_n|u-v|\) and
	\[
	\bigl|\sqrt{2b_{i1}p_n(u)^{r_{i1}}}
	-\sqrt{2b_{i1}p_n(v)^{r_{i1}}}\bigr|^2
	\le C_n|u-v|^2.
	\]
	Since \(\int_0^\infty(z^2\wedge z)\mu_i(\,\mathrm d z)<\infty\), by \cite[Lemma~A.1]{JiXiongXuYang2026}, there exists a
	pathwise unique \(\mathbb R^2\)-valued strong c\`adl\`ag truncated
	solution \(Z^{(n)}=(X^{(n)},Y^{(n)})\).
	Construct these solutions with the same initial state and
	driving noises. For \(m\ge n\), let
	\(\sigma_n^{(m)}:=\inf\{t\ge0:Z_t^{(m)}\notin D_n\}\).
	Then by pathwise uniqueness, we have $
	\sigma_n^{(m)}=\sigma_n^{(n)}=:\sigma_n,$ and $
Z_{t\wedge\sigma_n}^{(m)}=Z_{t\wedge\sigma_n}^{(n)}$ for $t \ge 0.$
	Consequently, $
	\sigma_n\uparrow\tau_0\wedge\tau_\infty$ and $Z_t:=Z_t^{(n)}$ if $t<\sigma_n$, which
	defines the pathwise unique strong c\`adl\`ag  solution.
	
	For \(i=1,2\) and \(u\ge0\), the one-dimensional localization
	in \cite[Theorem~3.1(i)]{LiYangZhou2019}, with absorption at
	zero, gives the axis process \(U^{(i)}\) satisfying
	\[
		U_t^{(i)}= u-b_{i0}\int_0^t(U_s^{(i)})^{r_{i0}}\,\mathrm d s
		+\int_0^t\sqrt{2b_{i1}(U_s^{(i)})^{r_{i1}}}\,\mathrm d B_i(s) +\int_0^t\int_0^\infty
		\int_0^{b_{i2}(U_{s-}^{(i)})^{r_{i2}}}
		z\,\widetilde N_i(\,\mathrm d s,\,\mathrm d z,\,\mathrm d v),
	\]
	up to its explosion time. In fact, by
	\cite[Theorem~2.8(i)]{LiYangZhou2019}, one can see that the axis processes are conservative.
On \(\{\tau_0<\tau_\infty\}\), we restart the axis equations
from \(X_{\tau_0}\) and \(Y_{\tau_0}\) by using the shifted
driving noises, and define
\[
Z_{\tau_0+t}:=(U_t^{(1)},U_t^{(2)}),\qquad t\ge0.
\]
Since zero is absorbing for each axis process, this gives
the continuation in \Cref{def:coordinatewise}.
Boundary initial states are treated with \(\tau_0=0\),
and the origin $(0, 0)$ is absorbing. On
\(\{\tau_\infty\le\tau_0\}\), the process is killed at
\(\tau_\infty\).
By \cite[Theorem~4.4.2]{EthierKurtz1986}, by the uniqueness in law
for the interior and absorbed axis processes, together
with localization, there is a Borel strong Markov family
with lifetime \(\tau_\infty\).
If \eqref{eq:model} is source-conservative, the conservativeness
of the axis processes implies that the continuation is
conservative. This completes the proof.

label: eq:imm-truncated-model
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \((x_0,y_0)\in E\). For \(m\ge1\), let
	\(p_m(u):=u^+\wedge m\) and consider the truncated equation
	\begin{equation}
		\left\{
		\begin{aligned}
			X_t^{(m)}={}&x_0+\int_0^t
			\bigl[\iota_1+a_1p_m(X_s^{(m)})^{\theta_1}
			p_m(Y_s^{(m)})^{\kappa_1}
			-b_{10}p_m(X_s^{(m)})^{r_{10}}\bigr]\,\mathrm d s\\
			&+\int_0^t
			\sqrt{2b_{11}p_m(X_{s-}^{(m)})^{r_{11}}}\,\mathrm d B_1(s)
			+\int_0^t\int_0^\infty
			\int_0^{b_{12}p_m(X_{s-}^{(m)})^{r_{12}}}
			z\,\widetilde N_1(\,\mathrm d s,\,\mathrm d z,\,\mathrm d u),\\
			Y_t^{(m)}={}&y_0+\int_0^t
			\bigl[\iota_2+a_2p_m(Y_s^{(m)})^{\theta_2}
			p_m(X_s^{(m)})^{\kappa_2}
			-b_{20}p_m(Y_s^{(m)})^{r_{20}}\bigr]\,\mathrm d s\\
			&+\int_0^t
			\sqrt{2b_{21}p_m(Y_{s-}^{(m)})^{r_{21}}}\,\mathrm d B_2(s)
			+\int_0^t\int_0^\infty
			\int_0^{b_{22}p_m(Y_{s-}^{(m)})^{r_{22}}}
			z\,\widetilde N_2(\,\mathrm d s,\,\mathrm d z,\,\mathrm d u).
		\end{aligned}
		\right.
		\label{eq:imm-truncated-model}
	\end{equation}
The truncated drift, covariance matrix and jump rates are
bounded and continuous, and
\(\int_0^\infty(z^2\wedge z)\mu_i(\,\mathrm d z)<\infty\).
By \cite[Theorem~2.2]{Stroock1975}, the martingale
problem associated with \eqref{eq:imm-truncated-model}
has a solution on \(D([0,\infty),\mathbb R^2)\). By
\cite[Theorem~2.3]{Kurtz2011}, on an enlarged
probability space, there exists an adapted c\`adl\`ag weak solution
\(Z^{(m)}=(X^{(m)},Y^{(m)})\) of
\eqref{eq:imm-truncated-model}.
	For each active Brownian coefficient and \(u,v\in[0,R]\),
	\begin{eqnarray*}
		\bigl|\sqrt{2b_{i1}u^{r_{i1}}}
		-\sqrt{2b_{i1}v^{r_{i1}}}\bigr|^2
		\le2b_{i1}|u^{r_{i1}}-v^{r_{i1}}|
		\le C_R|u-v|.
		\end{eqnarray*}
	Moreover, there exists a constant $C_m > 0$ such that $
	2b_{i1}p_m(u)^{r_{i1}}\le C_m u^+$ for $u \in \mathbb R$.
	Since \(\int_{0+}(C_m u)^{-1}\,\mathrm d u=\infty\), by the
	zero-local-time criterion, one can check that
	\(L_t^0(X^{(m)})=L_t^0(Y^{(m)})=0\).
	On \(\{X_{s-}^{(m)}\le0\}\), the noise coefficients vanish
	and the drift equals \(\iota_1\).
	All jumps of \(X^{(m)}\) are nonnegative, and no jump occurs
	when \(X_{s-}^{(m)}\le0\).
By Tanaka's
	formula, almost surely for every \(t\ge0\),
	\begin{align*}
		0\le(X_t^{(m)})^-
		&=(x_0)^-
		-\int_0^t\1_{\{X_{s-}^{(m)}\le0\}}\,\mathrm d X_s^{(m)}
		+\frac12L_t^0(X^{(m)})\\
		&\quad+\sum_{0<s\le t}
		\Bigl[(X_s^{(m)})^--(X_{s-}^{(m)})^-
		+\1_{\{X_{s-}^{(m)}\le0\}}
		(X_s^{(m)}-X_{s-}^{(m)})\Bigr]\\
		&=-\iota_1\int_0^t
		\1_{\{X_{s-}^{(m)}\le0\}}\,\mathrm d s\le0.
	\end{align*}
	Thus \((X_t^{(m)})^-=0\) for every \(t\ge0\), almost surely.
	The same argument gives \((Y_t^{(m)})^-=0\).	Thus \(Z^{(m)}\) takes values in \(E\).
	
	We next prove pathwise uniqueness. The truncated drift is
	globally Lipschitz, and, for \(u,v\in\mathbb R\),
	\[
	b_{i2}|p_m(u)^{r_{i2}}-p_m(v)^{r_{i2}}|
	\le C_m|u-v|.
	\]
	Let \(Z^{(m)}\) and \(\widetilde Z^{(m)}\) be two solutions
	of \eqref{eq:imm-truncated-model} driven by the same noises, and let $\Delta X^{(m)}:=X^{(m)}-\widetilde X^{(m)},$ $
	\Delta Y^{(m)}:=Y^{(m)}-\widetilde Y^{(m)}$ and $D_t^{(m)}:=|\Delta X_t^{(m)}|+|\Delta Y_t^{(m)}|.$
	By the same zero-local-time criterion, one can check that
	\(L_t^0(\Delta X^{(m)})=L_t^0(\Delta Y^{(m)})=0\).
	Applying Tanaka's formula and taking expectations, as in
	\cite[Proposition~3.1]{LiMytnik2011}, we have
	\[
	\mathbb E D_t^{(m)}\le D_0^{(m)}
	+C_m\int_0^t\mathbb E D_s^{(m)}\,\mathrm d s.
	\]
It follows that $\mathbb E D_t^{(m)}\le\mathrm e^{C_mt}D_0^{(m)}$.
	By \cite[Theorems~1 and~2]{BarczyLiPap2015},
	\eqref{eq:imm-truncated-model} therefore has a pathwise unique
	adapted strong c\`adl\`ag solution for every \(m\).
	
	For later use, the same argument applies to two solutions
	\(Z=(X,Y)\) and \(\widetilde Z=(\widetilde X,\widetilde Y)\)
	of \eqref{eq:model}, driven by the same noises, with initial
	states \((x_0,y_0)\) and \((\widetilde x_0,\widetilde y_0)\).
	For
	\(R>x_0\vee y_0\vee\widetilde x_0\vee\widetilde y_0\), let
	\[
	\sigma_R:=\inf\{t\ge0:
	X_t\vee Y_t\vee\widetilde X_t\vee\widetilde Y_t\ge R\},
	\qquad D_t:=|X_t-\widetilde X_t|+|Y_t-\widetilde Y_t|.
	\]
	By Gronwall's inequality, it gives that
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb E D_{t\wedge\sigma_R}\le\mathrm e^{C_Rt}D_0,
		\qquad t\ge0.
		\label{eq:stopped-L1-continuity}
	\end{equation}
	In particular, pathwise uniqueness holds up to the explosion
	time. 
As in the proof of \Cref{prop:axis-realization},
we construct all \(Z^{(m)}\) with the same initial state and
driving noises, and $\rho_n^{(m)}:=\inf\{t\ge0:
X_t^{(m)}\vee Y_t^{(m)}\ge n\}$ for $m\ge n>x_0\vee y_0.$
By \eqref{eq:stopped-L1-continuity},
\(\rho_n^{(m)}=\rho_n^{(n)}\) and the stopped solutions
are consistent. The same patching argument shows that $
\tau_\infty:=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho_n^{(n)}$ and $Z_t:=Z_t^{(n)}$ if $t<\rho_n^{(n)}$
defines an \(E\)-valued strong c\`adl\`ag solution of
\eqref{eq:model} on \([0,\tau_\infty)\). Then
pathwise uniqueness follows from
\eqref{eq:stopped-L1-continuity} by letting \(R\to\infty\).
